sections.title: Agent notifications and proactivity QA
sections.text:
Sagax treats proactivity as an explicit trigger, not as a hidden
heartbeat. A bot may continue within an active task through Auto mode, may be
started by a Routine or Webhook, and may coordinate peers when its engine and
profile allow that. With Proactive on (the default), the bot also wakes on a
real inbound event Sagax already receives (email, calendar, failed run, bot
mention, webhook post); it does not invent work by polling. Off disables
those wakes.

sections.title: Agent notifications and proactivity QA: Automated coverage
sections.text:
| Contract | Test |
 
| Per-agent off means quiet; empty completions stay quiet; summaries are bounded | `server/notify.test.ts` |
| Browser click returns the exact bot/task target | `src/lib/notify.test.ts` |
| Store navigation selects the bot and switches the task | `src/state/store.test.ts` |
| Routine failure receipt and callback occur once | `server/routines.test.ts` |
| Real failed routine emits one `routine-failed` notification and no duplicate `done` | `server/notification-wiring.test.ts` |
| iOS target parsing and detached-task decision | `ios/Tests/CompanionCoreTests/DecodingTests.swift` |
| Paired-device route policy remains default-deny | `companion/test/routes.test.ts` |

sections.title: Agent notifications and proactivity QA: Manual release pass
sections.text:
Run these with two bots, notifications enabled on one and disabled on the
other:
1. Background the desktop window. Complete a normal task and confirm one
 result notification. Click it and verify the exact task opens.
2. Trigger an approval and a question. Confirm their copy, click targets, and
 that no duplicate completion notification appears before the task settles.
3. Run a routine manually, then create a controlled failing run. Confirm the
 receipt shows the detached task and the failure generates exactly one alert.
4. Repeat the above with notifications disabled for that bot; the chat and run
 receipt should update without a system alert.
5. On iOS, tap a live/replayed notification for a non-active routine task.
 Confirm the app switches the server-side active task before navigating.
6. Exercise Auto mode, a Routine, and a Webhook independently. Verify each has
 a visible initiating user/configured trigger and that no unconfigured
 heartbeat starts work.
Live provider, OS-permission, backgrounding, and APNs behavior cannot be proven
by unit tests alone and remains part of the signed desktop/iPhone release pass.

sections.title: Agent notifications and proactivity QA: Notification policy
sections.text:
The harness is the single owner of interruption policy. A bot with
notifications disabled remains quiet. Otherwise it may emit:
- Needs approval or has a question when the task is blocked on the user.
- Needs your hands when a computer task requires a takeover.
- Finished only when there is a non-empty result to summarize.
- Routine failed when a scheduled or manual routine run cannot complete.
Every notification carries both the bot ID and the exact task thread ID. A
click must select that bot and switch to that task, including a routine's
detached task; opening whichever task happens to be active is a failure.
Desktop notifications are suppressed while the window already has focus. The
iOS app can present live or replayed notifications while it is running and uses
the same bot/task target when the notification is tapped. Waking a terminated
iOS app still requires a future APNs relay; local network or VPN connectivity
alone cannot provide closed-app delivery.

sections.title: API document for one person
sections.text:
Paste an OpenAPI 3 document. The bots of that person, in a conversation
with them, receive one tool per operation. Other members do not. There is
no admin switch.
 
`headers` are sealed with the vault key (AES-256-GCM, mode 0600) in
`openapi.enc`, or under `principals/ /` on an organization server.
They are never listed back and they are not part of a workspace backup.
A room does not receive the tools. Since 2026-10-28 a bot shared with a
person offers that person their own operations, never its owner's: a
conversation uses the credentials of who speaks, and a routine those of
its owner. Someone with no document gets no tool, and a stale call is
refused with a sentence that says they have none.
The document must be OpenAPI 3 with the operations written inline.
References are not expanded. At most 40 operations. The host is resolved
once. Every address is checked, and the connection uses that address, so
a later DNS answer cannot move the call. On an organization server the
address has to be on the public internet. Metadata, link-local and
reserved addresses are refused everywhere. A redirect is not followed.
The answer is read up to 64 KB and wrapped as untrusted data.
A GET is a read. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE follow the person's approval
level: they are not pre-allowed on the agents server, so Ask shows a card.
`openapi_*` is an `own` permission, the same tier as `vault_http_request`,
so the MCP guard does not refuse the call as an unknown tool.
Routines are not involved. The call is an HTTP request, not a model turn.

sections.title: OpenCode: Models
sections.text:
The model picker runs `opencode models --verbose` against the configured binary
and preserves every exact `provider/model` ID returned by the CLI. This can
include Zen (`opencode/*`), Go (`opencode-go/*`), third-party providers, custom
configuration, and local endpoints. If discovery temporarily fails, the last
successful catalog is used, followed by a small anonymous-model fallback.
Before every prompt, ACP receives `session/set_config_option` with
`configId: "model"` and the exact selected provider-qualified model ID.

sections.title: OpenCode
sections.text:
OpenCode is an optional Sagax engine. Sagax runs the maintained
OpenCode CLI through its ACP stdio interface, so sessions, streaming, coding
tools, permission requests, MCP integrations, resume, and cancellation use the
same runtime as the other ACP engines.

sections.title: OpenCode: Setup
sections.text:
1. Install the official CLI using the
 OpenCode installation guide.
2. Connect the providers you want in the OpenCode app, run
 `opencode auth login`, or save the provider's key in Sagax under
 Settings → API keys → Keys for other OpenCode providers. On an OMB
 Cloud, which has no terminal, save the key there.
3. Restart Sagax. It reuses OpenCode's existing connections and model
 configuration automatically.
For OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, DeepSeek, Cline or your own provider, see
Other model providers.
OpenCode includes anonymous free models. A Zen, Go, OpenRouter, or other
provider connection expands the catalog according to the installed CLI. An
OpenCode API key can optionally be stored under Settings → API keys. It is
write-only and injected as `OPENCODE_API_KEY` only into the OpenCode child
process; it is not sent to the renderer, logs, analytics, snapshots, error
messages, or command arguments.
Keys for OpenCode's other providers go under Keys for other OpenCode
providers in the same place, each under the environment name OpenCode reads
it from: `VENICE_API_KEY` for Venice, `GROQ_API_KEY` for Groq, and so on. This
works on the desktop and on My Cloud, where there is no terminal to export
them in. Each key is write-only (Settings shows its name, never the key), is
kept in the server's own config, and is passed only to the OpenCode process;
saving one reloads the engines, so OpenCode lists that provider's models
straight away. On a Cloud, a hosted team or an organization's desktop,
OpenCode still never reads provider keys from the server's own environment;
the keys saved here are the exception. Names Sagax keeps for itself
(`OPENCODE_*`, `SAGAX_*`, and the keys it saves for other engines, such as
`XAI_API_KEY`) are refused, and up to 20 keys can be saved.
Sagax does not copy or rewrite `auth.json`. The OpenCode CLI remains the
owner of provider authentication, and the same Zen or Go connection used by
the OpenCode desktop/TUI is used by Sagax.

sections.title: OpenCode: Testing
sections.text:
Normal unit and ACP protocol tests do not require a subscription. Live tests
must be explicitly enabled and must never print credentials or upload native
protocol logs from a credentialed run.

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Approvals
sections.text:
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET approvals` | employee | the cards the caller may decide (unchanged) |
| `GET approvals?scope=org` | admin | every pending card of the organization |
| `GET approvals/history?q&limit&cursor` | admin | decided cards of the last 90 days |
| `POST approvals/{thread}/{request}` | employee | allow or deny (unchanged) |
`GET approvals?scope=org` answers `{approvals}` in the shape of `GET
approvals`, at most 2,000, oldest first; `decidable` is true only on a card
this admin may answer here (an admin card, or a card of their own bot, a
plain tool card on the fleet host). An owner card of someone else's bot is
listed, never decidable.
### `GET approvals/history`
 
From the decision log: the cards a person answered (in Sagax or from the
console), and since 2026-10-11 the permission cards nobody answered before
their own timeout (`decision: "expired"`, `by` null), newest first. `by`
names the person when Sagax knows them, else the device label. A card that
expired before that day has no row.
### Organization approval rules (2026-10-21)
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET org-approvals` | admin | `{ alwaysAllow, rules }` |
| `POST org-approvals` | admin | `{ alwaysAllow: true \| false }` |
| `POST org-approvals/rules` | admin | `{ when, behavior: "ask" \| "deny" }`, 201 `{ rule }` |
| `POST org-approvals/rules/{id}` | admin | `{ when?, behavior?, enabled? }` |
| `POST org-approvals/rules/{id}/remove` | admin | remove one rule |
An organization rule is a custom rule in plain words
(`shared/custom-rules.ts`) that an admin writes for every person and every
bot of the server. It only restricts: Ask first or Refuse, never Allow
(400). It wins over a person's own rule of the same behavior, and members
see it in their bot's Rules card, marked "Required by your administrator",
without a way to change or remove it (`/api/custom-rules/:id` answers 403
`org_rule_locked`). A rule view is `{ id, when, behavior, enabled,
recognized, createdAt, updatedAt }`; `recognized` false means the words name
nothing the reviewer can test, so the rule holds nothing. At most 100.
`alwaysAllow` false (on by default) turns "Always allow" off for everyone:
an Allow answers that one card. Every answer that would save a standing
grant (a session allow, a saved command, an Always allow rule or key) is
refused with 403 `org_always_allow_off`, no allow rule is saved or turned
on, and the standing grants people already saved stop answering while it is
off (they answer again when it is back on). Each change is an `approval`
row of the admin activity (`org.approvals.*`). Kept in
`custom-approval-rules.json` under `org`; `server/custom-rules-org.ts`.

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Bots
sections.text:
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET bots/{id}` | manager | a bot's page |
| `GET bots/{id}/avatar` | manager | the bot's uploaded picture |
| `GET bots/{id}/capabilities` | manager | the bot's capabilities, read only |
| `POST bots/{id}/clone` | manager (bot and new owner in reach) | a copy for its owner or another person |
| `POST bots/{id}/archive` | manager in reach, admin | archive |
| `POST bots/{id}/restore` | manager in reach, admin | restore |
| `POST bots/{id}/transfer` | admin | another owner |
| `POST bots/{id}/model` | manager in reach, admin | another engine or model |
| `POST bots/{id}/stop` | admin | stop every running turn, task and routine run |
| `POST bots/{id}/delete` | admin | delete, with the bot's name as confirmation |
| `POST bots/bulk` | admin | archive, restore, transfer or model on 1 to 100 bots |
| `GET bots/{id}/package` | admin | the package document, secrets redacted; `?format=zip`: the whole bot as a zip |
| `POST bots/import` | admin | a package or a bot zip becomes bots of a chosen owner |
### `GET bots/{id}`
 
The AdminBot fields of `GET bots`, plus the facts above. `soul.summary` is
the first line of the instructions (at most 140 characters), never the
instructions themselves; no message, memory or routine prompt is answered.
### A bot's look and persona
`look` is what the bot wears, as the app resolves it
(`server/org-admin-look.ts`, the rule of `src/components/Avatar.tsx`); the
console draws the character itself from it.
- `kind`: `image` when the bot has an uploaded picture shown with a photo
 crop (`GET bots/{id}/avatar` serves it); `mascot` when its owner chose a
 character or a skin; `default` when they chose nothing: the owl in the
 bot's color, as every bot wore before. The character fields are always
 there: they are what the app draws when the picture fails to load.
- `character`: `owl`, `crab`, `shape`, `trombi`, `bunbu`, `shiba`,
 `grump`, `ogre` or `frog`. `family`: `classics` (owl, trombi), `shapes`
 (shape) or `animals` (crab, bunbu, shiba, grump, ogre, frog).
- `color`: the bot's color name (`shared/mascot-colors.ts`, six palettes);
 `colorHex` its value, null for a name this server does not know. Trombi
 ignores it.
- `skin`: the character's skin. The owl's is the bot's owl skin (`none`,
 `snowy`, `barn`, `carbon`, `gold`, `frost`, `neon`, `lightning`,
 `chrome`, `inferno`, `holo`, `galaxy`, `spirit`); the other characters'
 are listed per character in `GET capabilities` `mascots[].skins`
 (shape: `plain` ... `galaxy`; trombi: `classic` ... `molten`; bunbu,
 shiba, grump, ogre, frog and crab: `plain`, their own coats, then the
 premium set). An older stored name reads as its current id.
- `shape`: the shape character's shape, one of `MASCOT_SHAPES`
 (shared/mascot-look.ts: `circle`, `bean` the pebble, `squircle`, `pill`
 the capsule, `pick` the triangle, `hexagon`, `cloud`, `drop` the teardrop,
 `pumpkin` and the others of the set), else null.

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Computers
sections.text:
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET computers?kind&state&owner&q&limit&cursor` | admin | every server environment and every connected desktop |
| `GET computers/{id}` | admin | one computer and its recent activity |
| `POST computers/{id}/start`, `stop`, `pause`, `resume`, `update` | admin | power and rebuild a server environment (`{}`, or `{"confirm": true}` while a bot works there) |
| `POST computers/{id}/reset`, `delete` | admin | erase a server environment (`{"confirm": true}` required) |
A person reaches their own server environment without the admin role
(2026-10-26): `GET computers`, `GET computers/{id}` and `POST
computers/{id}/start`, `stop`, `pause`, `resume`, `reset` accept an
assertion with the person's own role and a `grant` claim `{ "kind":
"own-computer", "method", "path" }` bound to that very request (`path`
below `/api/org/admin/`, no query; any other shape refuses the assertion).
The route then answers only the person's own computers: the list keeps
them, anyone else's computer is `404 not_found`. `update` and `delete`
take no grant and stay an admin's. Perspicax signs the grant only after
it has checked the owner itself.
The same mechanism covers a person's own bots and routines (2026-10-26), so
no call of a member is ever signed above their own role:
| Grant kind | Routes | Answered |
 
| `own-bot` | `GET bots`, `GET bots/{id}`, `bots/{id}/avatar`, `bots/{id}/package`, `bots/{id}/capabilities`, `files/{bot}/roots\|list\|stat\|read\|download`, `POST bots/{id}/clone\|archive\|restore\|model\|stop\|delete`, `GET usage`, `GET incidents`, `GET logs`, `GET audit?target= ` | the person's own bots only (not one shared with them); a copy stays theirs (another owner `403`); usage rows, incidents and log lines of their own bots; the activity of one bot of theirs (`target` required) |
| `own-routine` | `GET routines`, `GET routines/{id}`, `GET routines/{id}/runs`, `POST routines/{id}/run\|pause` | the routines of the person's own bots |
The transfer, `bots/bulk`, `bots/import` and every other route take no
grant.
Code: `server/org-admin-computers.ts`. A server environment is the
organization's machine for one person (sagax-sandboxd,
`docs/user-sandbox.md`): an admin acts on it with the calls the person's
own Computer tab makes. A desktop computer is the person's own (the Sagax
app signed in to this server, the desktop bridge): it is listed read only,
by its name, platform, presence and last contact, and never acted on; the
console never reaches its files, its system facts or its Local VM.
### `GET computers`
- `id`: `env: ` for a server environment, `desktop:<16 hex>`
 for a desktop (a digest of its person and the app's own id, which never
 reaches the wire). Stable while the desktop stays registered.
- `kind`: `server-environment` or `desktop`. `name`: the owner's name for
 an environment, the name the Sagax app registered (`os.hostname()`) for a
 desktop.
- `state`: a server environment is `running`, `paused`, `stopped` or

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Connections
sections.text:
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET connections` | admin | engines, people's connections, MCP servers, marketplaces, skills library |
| `POST connections/test` | admin | test one line |
### `GET connections`
- `engines[].people`: active people whose own turns can run on the engine
 (subscription, key or organization key). `orgKey` says whether the
 organization's key is set, never the key.
- `people[].engines[].ok` and `checkedAt` stay null: Sagax does not check a
 person's engine in the background; `POST connections/test` with
 `principalId` does it on demand.
- `skills`: the organization's skills library (empty while the library is
 off); `version` is the first 12 hex of the skill's SHA-256.
### `POST connections/test`
 `{ "kind": "engine", "id": "claude", "principalId": "pr_7c1e..." }` 
Answers `{ok, latencyMs, reason, label}`, for example
`{"ok": false, "latencyMs": 12, "reason": "no_access", "label": "This person has no access to this engine (...)"}`.
- `engine`: the engine answers its probe (and, with `principalId`, that
 person can run on it).
- `mcp`: a remote MCP server (the organization's, or the person's with
 `principalId`) answers over HTTP with a status below 500. No credential is
 sent. A server started by command (stdio) is started with its configured
 arguments and variables (the organization's on this host, a person's in
 their server environment), must answer the MCP `initialize` handshake and
 `tools/list` within 8 s, and is stopped after. Success:
 `{"ok": true, "reason": null, "label": "The server answered with 12 tools."}`.
 A failure names its cause in `reason`: `spawn_failed`, `exited` (the label
 carries the exit code), `handshake_refused`, `tools_refused`, `protocol`,
 `timeout`, `environment_refused` or `no_environment`. No variable value,
 argument or stderr line is ever in the answer or the log.
- `marketplace`: its address (or `https://github.com/ `) answers.
Each test has 10 s. Audited `connections.test`.

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Link routes (`/api/org/link/*`)
sections.text:
Routes Perspicax calls on its own behalf, not for a person: their only
credential is the link token Perspicax wrote to this server's link file
(`SAGAX_PERSPICAX_LINK_FILE`, the `link_token` field), never a console
assertion. Code: `server/org-link-routes.ts`.
| Method and path | Credential | What |
 
| `POST /api/org/link/directory-refresh` | link token | read the directory now |
### `POST /api/org/link/directory-refresh`
 
Sagax re-reads the directory (`GET /api/v1/pulsabot/directory`) every
`SAGAX_PERSPICAX_DIRECTORY_SECONDS` (300 by default), so a rights change
made in Perspicax (a permission set or its assignment, `sagax_bots`, a
team, a profile, a role) reached Sagax up to five
minutes later. Perspicax calls this route right after such a change, and
Sagax fetches the directory at once. Call it once per change; no body.
- Answers `202 {"ok": true, "refresh": "started"}`, or `"queued"` when a
 fetch is running or one started less than 2 s ago: exactly one more fetch
 then follows, so a change committed during a running fetch is still read.
 The fetch runs after the answer; its outcome is in the server log and in
 `GET overview` like a poll's. Nothing else is written.
- `401 {"error": "unauthorized"}` for a missing or wrong token, a token sent
 any other way than `Authorization: Bearer` (query, Basic, cookie) included.
 A token Perspicax just rotated is accepted: a mismatch re-reads the link
 file once.
- `429 {"error": "rate_limited"}` with `Retry-After: 60` after 10 failed
 authentications from one socket address in 60 s (even with the good token
 until the window passes), or beyond 60 accepted calls in a minute.
- `404 {"error": "not_found"}` on a solo server or an organization server
 with no link file; `405` for another method.
- Every answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.
Perspicax holds the link token only where it writes the link file itself
(the server of `pulsabot_origin` with `PXC_PULSABOT_LINK_FILE`); a server
linked from the console keeps the poll and the refresh at each sign-in.

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Logs
sections.text:
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET logs?level&limit&before` | admin | the server log tail |
| `GET incidents?kind&q&limit&cursor` | admin | failed, stalled and unstartable runs, failed routines |
| `GET audit` | admin | the admin activity log (above) |
### `GET logs`
`level` is `info`, `warn` or `error` (that level and above), `limit` 1 to 500
(default 200), `before` the `seq` of a line (the `next` of the last page).
 
The last 2,000 lines the server wrote to its console, each at most 2,000
characters, secrets redacted when captured (`redactSecretsInText`). Since
2026-10-11 the window also lives on disk (` /server-log/`, two files of
at most 2 MiB each, mode 0600, left out of workspace backups), so a restart
keeps the last lines and `seq` keeps growing across restarts; the answer's
shape is unchanged. The container's log driver keeps the whole log.
### `GET incidents`
`kind` is `failed`, `stalled`, `could-not-start` or `routine-failed`; the
last 90 days, newest first.
 
From the problem log (` /problems/`, 180 days): every incident Sagax
reports to a Primary Bot, written before its delivery rules. `detail` is the
cause the person reads in the thread (redacted, at most 300 characters),
never a message; a routine failure carries `routineId`.

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`)
sections.text:
The API the Perspicax console reads through its proxy to administer a Sagax
organization server. Design: Perspicax
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-sagax-admin-console-design.md`, section 5.
Code: `server/org-admin-routes.ts` (the gate and the first routes),
`server/org-admin-console.ts` (the route table, paging, refusals) and one
module per area (`server/org-admin-*.ts`).

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): People
sections.text:
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET people?q&role&presence&disabled&limit&cursor` | manager | every person of the organization in reach |
| `GET people/{principal}` | manager | a person's page |
| `POST people/{principal}/disable` | admin | turn a person off or on in this Sagax |
| `POST people/{principal}/reset-access` | admin | delete their engine sign-ins, end their sessions |
| `POST people/{principal}/connections/revoke` | admin | remove their own connections |
| `POST people/{principal}/routines/pause` | admin | pause every routine that runs as them |
| `POST people/{principal}/routines/resume` | admin | resume every routine that runs as them |
### `GET people`
`role` is `admin` or `member`, `presence` one of `online`, `idle`, `away`,
`offline`, `disabled` `true` or `false`, `q` searches the name and the
Perspicax user id.
- `disabledBy`: `perspicax` when Perspicax says the person is out,
 `sagax` when an admin turned them off here, null otherwise.
- `routines`: the routines that run as this person.
- `turns30d`, `costUsd30d`, `lastTurnAt`: the turns this person spoke (a
 routine counts for the person it ran as) over the last 30 days.
- `engines[].via`: what their own turns run with on each engine:
 `subscription` (their own sign-in here), `key` (their model key in
 Perspicax, named by provider only), `org-key`, or `none`.
### `GET people/{principal}`
The row above, plus:
 
`permissions` (2026-10-09) is what this server enforces for the person:
`source` is `admin` (every key), `perspicax` (the list the directory sent,
unknown and admin-only keys dropped) or `defaults` (Perspicax sent none: the
member defaults). `narrowedBy` names the person sheet settings applied on top
(`sagax_bots` when it says use only). The Perspicax field
`sagax_integrations` is ignored since 2026-10-30: `apps.ownIntegrations` is
the only rule for a person's own plugins, skills and MCP servers.
`mcpServers[].state` is `enabled` or `disabled`.
### `POST people/{principal}/disable`
 `{ "disabled": true, "reason": "Contract ended" }` 
Answers `{person}` (the row). Disabling ends every session of the person at
once; while disabled no request of theirs is served (401
`principal_disabled`), a new sign-in is refused at its first request, their
routines do not run, and a console assertion naming them is refused. It is
independent of Perspicax's own disable: a sign-in does not clear it, only
`{"disabled": false}` does. An admin cannot disable themselves (409 `self`).
Audited `person.console_disable` and `person.console_enable`.
### `POST people/{principal}/reset-access`
 `{ "scope": "engine-logins" }` 
`scope` is `engine-logins` (delete the person's subscription sign-ins on
this server), `sessions` (end every session; they sign in again) or `all`.
Answers `{person, cleared: {engineLogins, sessions}}`. Audited
`person.reset_access`.
### `POST people/{principal}/connections/revoke`
The body of the session route: `{"all": true}`, `{"kind": "mcp", "name"}`,

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Routes
sections.text:
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET capabilities` | employee | the release, every route this server serves and the permission catalogue |
| `GET overview` | manager | health, engines, sandboxes, presence, turns, routines, errors, latency, host, deploy, backup |
| `GET bots` | manager | every bot in reach; paged and filtered when asked |
| `GET usage?from&to` | manager | usage per day, bot, speaker and engine |
| `GET approvals` | employee | the cards the caller may decide |
| `POST approvals/{thread}/{request}` | employee | `{decision: "allow" or "deny"}` |
| `GET audit?from&to&limit&before&category&target` | admin | the admin activity log, newest first |
| `GET files/{bot}/roots,list,stat,read,download` | manager | a bot's files, read only |
### `GET capabilities`
 `GET /api/org/admin/capabilities` 
 
`version` is the Sagax release people know (`package.json` `forkVersion`, or
`SAGAX_RELEASE_VERSION`), not the base version the link sends. `api` is 1 for
a server that predates this route (it answers `404 not_found`), 2 since
the console routes, 3 since the permission catalogue, 4 since `engines`
(both 2026-10-09) and 5 since the bots' `look` and `persona` with `mascots`
(2026-10-11). A route
missing from `routes` is not offered by this server: the console says so
instead of calling it.
`permissions` is the permission catalogue of this server
(`shared/permissions.ts`, spec
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-sagax-permission-matrix.md`): one row per
key, in catalogue order, with its group, English and French label and
description, whether a plain member holds it when Perspicax sends no list
(`memberDefault`), and whether only an organization admin may hold it
(`adminOnly`, with `adminOnlyReason`). Perspicax draws its permission matrix
from these rows and sends back, in the directory, each person's effective
keys (`permissions` on the person: the union of the default permission
set, the permission sets given to the person and those of their teams,
every key for an admin; `sagax_permission_sets` names those sets for
display, and a profile's `sagax_permissions` is null since Perspicax 0051). Keys are stable; a server that predates the
catalogue answers without `permissions`.
`engines` lists every engine (model provider) of this server, from the same
catalogue as Sagax's model picker: `id` is the engine instance id that
`allowedEngines` takes, `name` the name the picker shows, `kind` the group the
picker's provider column puts it in (`local` for a custom engine such as a
local model server, `cloud` for a subscription or API key engine),
`installed` whether it runs on this server, and `auth` how a person gets
access (`oauth`: a sign-in with the provider's account, `apiKey`: a key,
`none`: nothing to sign in to). A server before api 4 answers without
`engines`. Since 2026-10-16 each engine also says `orgKey`: the
organization's key serves it (never the key), and when the organization

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Routines
sections.text:
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET routines?q&status&bot&owner&limit&cursor` | manager | every routine in reach |
| `GET routines/{id}` | manager | one routine |
| `GET routines/{id}/runs?limit&cursor` | manager | its runs, newest first |
| `GET routines/runs?from&to&scope&bot&routine&state&q&limit&cursor` | employee | the calendar: every run in a window, past and planned |
| `POST routines/{id}/run` | manager in reach, admin | run now |
| `POST routines/{id}/pause` | manager in reach, admin | pause or resume |
A manager reaches a routine whose bot owner or whose runner is in their
reach. No routine prompt, run output or message is ever answered.
The Automations page of Sagax itself (2026-10-09) widens its own view with
two permissions of the catalogue, independent of this console route:
`routines.viewTeam` (the routines of the people in the caller's teams and of
the bots shared with those teams) and `routines.viewAll` (every routine of
the organization); an admin holds both, a member holds neither by default.
They gate `GET /api/routines?scope=mine|team|all&teamId&botId&ownerId&status`
and `DELETE /api/routine-runs?scope=...` on the Sagax server, not these
console routes, whose `status`, `bot` and `owner` filters already match
(`status` there is `enabled|paused|failing`, the Sagax page says
`active|paused|failing`). A console that wants a team filter can filter its
items by `owner.principalId` against the directory's teams; no new console
parameter is needed.
### `GET routines`
`status` is `enabled`, `paused` or `failing` (its last run failed); `bot` a
bot id; `owner` the bot owner's principal id or Perspicax user id.
- `schedule` is the schedule in words (times in the server's zone, `once`
 in UTC).
- `lastRun.status`: `ok` (completed), `failed`, `skipped` (cancelled or
 missed) or `running` (queued, running or waiting). `reason` is a code,
 `label` its readable words in the assertion's language.
- `suspended` (`person_out` or `no_right`) is present when Sagax paused the
 routine for its person.
### `GET routines/{id}/runs`
 
`turns` and `costUsd` come from the usage ledger (the run's own cost when
the run carries one). The thread opens in Sagax at
` /#thread= &bot= `.
### `GET routines/runs` (the calendar)
 `GET /api/org/admin/routines/runs?from=2026-10-05&to=2026-10-11&scope=all&limit=200` 
- `from` and `to`: milliseconds, an ISO date (`to` as a date covers that
 whole UTC day) or an ISO date and time; at most 92 days apart. Without
 them: the last 7 days and the next 7. The answer echoes the window in
 milliseconds.
- Items are every run that overlaps the window (started or scheduled
 before `to`, ended or still going after `from`), then the planned
 occurrences from now (or `from`, when later) to `to`, computed from each
 enabled routine's schedule in the routines' time zone; a suspended or
 paused routine plans nothing, and an occurrence already queued is listed
 once, as that run. Sorted by `startedAt`, then routine.

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Settings
sections.text:
| Method and path | Role | What |
 
| `GET settings` | admin | organization settings, policies, backup |
| `POST settings` | admin | change policies |
### `GET settings`
 
`org` is what `GET /api/org` answers as `settings` (no token).
`memberEnvironmentAutonomy` (on unless an admin turns it off, 2026-10-16): a
bot runs its owner's commands in the owner's own isolated environment (their
server environment, their Local VM) without a card
(approval levels).
`confidentialThreadsByDefault` (off unless an admin turns it on in Sagax,
Settings > Organisation, 2026-10-16): new threads start confidential
(confidential threads); read only here.
`memberAutoApproval` (on unless an admin turns it off, 2026-10-16): a bot a
member owns runs Approve for me and Auto-accept edits as such; off, they run
as Ask and a member cannot choose them
(approval levels).
The first time it is turned off, the levels members saved go back to Ask
once; turning it on again brings none back. `null` in a
policy list means any. `defaults` are the New bot defaults (engine, model,
approval level).
### `POST settings`
 `{ "allowFullAccess": false, "memberEnvironmentAutonomy": true, "memberAutoApproval": false, "pluginMarketplaces": { "mode": "list", "allow": ["acme/plugins", "acme/*"] }, "allowedEngines": ["claude"], "ownAccountsOutsideList": false, "defaults": { "engine": "claude", "model": "claude-opus-4-1", "approvalMode": "ask" }, "interimAttachDays": 0 }` 
Any subset. Answers `{settings}` (the GET shape). Refusals: 400
`bad_request` (an unknown field or value), 400 `engine_not_installed` (an
engine in `allowedEngines` this server does not have), 400 `invalid_policy`
(a marketplace entry). Each changed setting writes its own `org.settings`
row with its before and after.
`allowedEngines` (engine instance ids, `null` for every engine; an empty
list means no engine at all since 2026-10-17, Perspicax 1.8.34) is enforced
everywhere since 2026-10-09, and since 2026-10-30 for everyone: an admin
too, and whoever pays (the organization's key, or a person's own
subscription or key):
- The console's model changes (`POST bots/{id}/model`, bulk `model`) answer
 400 `engine_not_allowed`.
- Sagax refuses a model on another engine (a bot or thread model change
 answers 403) and a turn on one (409 `engine_not_allowed`); Auto never picks
 one.
- When the list changes (and at server start), a bot on an engine no longer
 allowed moves to Auto, based on the New bot default when its engine is
 allowed, else on the first allowed engine installed here; a thread's own
 model on such an engine follows its bot again.
- The list reaches every open Sagax app in its config (`allowedEngines`,
 refreshed live): the model picker, Settings > Models and New bot list
 only these providers and their models (`shared/offered-engines.ts`). A
 provider the person already connected but no longer allowed is not
 listed.
`ownAccountsOutsideList` (`false` unless an admin turns it on, 2026-10-30;

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): The gate
sections.text:
- Answered before the session gate and before loopback trust. The only
 credential is a console assertion Perspicax signs per request
 (`Authorization: Bearer `, `typ` `pulsabot-console+jwt`, at most
 120 s, single use `jti`, `server_id` equal to the link's, `act.sub`
 `console`). A session cookie is ignored here. An AI client's assertion
 (`act.sub` `perspicax-mcp`) is refused here: it opens the member API only
 (`docs/org-member-api.md`).
- The role is the assertion's Perspicax role: `admin`, `manager` or
 `employee`. A manager reads only their reach: themselves plus the people of
 the teams they manage, and the bots those people own or that are shared
 with them. Out of reach reads as `404 not_found`.
- An optional `locale` claim (`fr`, `en`, `fr-CA`) chooses the language of
 every readable `label`. English otherwise.
- Every answer carries `X-Sagax-Admin-Api: 1` and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- A refusal is `{code, message, reason, error}`: `reason` is the sentence the
 console shows (`message` and `error` carry the same text for older
 readers). A server fault is `500 server_error` with a generic sentence; its
 detail goes to the server log only.
- Lists page by an opaque cursor: `limit` (1 to 200, default 50), `cursor`
 (the `next` of the previous page) and `q` (search, at most 200
 characters). The answer is `{items, next}`; `next` is null on the last
 page.
- Every POST writes one row of the admin activity log, actor
 `{kind: "person", principalId, via: "console"}`, and answers the changed
 record.
- No answer carries a secret: model keys, tokens and passwords are named by
 provider or reported as set or not set, never shown.

sections.title: Organization admin API (`/api/org/admin/*`): Usage and cost
sections.text:
`GET usage` (above) carries `engine` on each row; the console groups by
engine, person, bot or day and exports CSV from the rows it holds.

sections.title: The organization library: Files
sections.text:
`DATA_DIR/org-library/`:
| File | Written by | What |
 
| `state.json` | runtime | The index of what was added (contract §3.4), plus `kind`, `name` and `withdrawnHandled` per install, and `adding`: team Adds that have started and not finished. Mode 0600. |
| `blobs/ .json` | Electron | Release bytes, checked on every read. |
| `catalog.json` | Electron | The last applied catalog body. The runtime does not read it. |
| `presets.json` | runtime (`server/presets.ts`) | Preset bots, from files and from installs here (presets.md). An install's presets are listed under `presets` in `state.json`. |
Preset rows in `presets.json` carry their install id too. They are how a
package of presets and skills (no bots) is recognized again if its
`state.json` entry is lost, and they give an adopted install its `presets`
back. They never keep a team added, and neither does a bot someone made from
one of its presets (nor that bot's skills, although they carry the install's
skill stamp marked `via: "preset"`), so a team the person deleted can be
added again; its presets are then refreshed in place, never duplicated.
New bot asks the library for each install's status
(`OrgLibrary.installStatuses()`), from its state in memory.
The records are the source of truth. `state.json` is rebuilt from them in
these cases:
- on start;
- before every Add;
- after each relayed catalog;
- whenever a bot or group chat is deleted, or a team is renamed.
A team's section is read from where its bots are now, so renaming the team
needs no hook. A team counts as added while any of its bots, group chats or
routines is left. An offered skill someone put on another bot is a copy: it
stays, but it does not keep the team added, so once the team's own records
are gone the install is `removed` and Add brings the whole team back.
Each install's `removedLocally` (contract §3.4) lists the parts of an added
team the person deleted: `agent: ` for a bot, `room: ` for a group
chat and `routine: ` for a routine. The automatic update (v1.1) reads it
to tell a part the person deleted from a part a new release adds, and never
brings a deleted part back. It is kept like this:
- When it is noted. Each time the index is rebuilt, a key the index held
 that no longer has a record is added to the list once. Rebuilding again,
 or restarting, adds nothing. A routine stops counting when its bot is
 deleted, so deleting a bot notes its routines too. Deleting a routine is
 not a store change, so it is noted at the next rebuild (the next catalog,
 Add or start).
- A team deleted whole becomes `removed`, and every one of its parts is
 noted too. The list then reads the same whether the person deleted the
 team at once or one bot at a time.
- A part that has a record again (records restored from a backup) is
 taken off the list, so it never names a part that is there.
- Add after a removal brings the whole team back, so it starts a new,
 empty list.

sections.title: The organization library: How the catalog arrives
sections.text:
This runtime never talks to Admin. Electron main (`electron/managed-desktop.mjs`)
owns the Admin connection: it fetches the catalog and each release file,
checks their SHA-256, and writes the files to
`DATA_DIR/org-library/blobs/ .json`. It then relays the catalog over
the private utility port:
- A catalog body sent as a string must hash to `digest`.
- The runtime reads the catalog as contract §5.3 defines it: unknown fields
 are ignored and a bad entry is dropped. A bad envelope, or a catalog for
 another organization, is refused (`ok: false`), and the last good catalog
 stays.
- `library: null` (sign-out, expiry or revocation) hides the shelf and
 changes nothing else.
- Release files are checked against their SHA-256 on every read, and never
 through a symbolic link. A file that does not match is treated as not
 downloaded.
After acknowledging, the runtime reconciles its index, handles withdrawn
releases, and sends a full snapshot back:
 
The runtime sends this snapshot at three points:
- after each relayed catalog;
- after each Add, whether it succeeds or fails;
- after the person deletes the last record of an install.
Debouncing, retries and the once-per-start report belong to Electron main.
A report lists only installs from the current organization. It never
contains names, paths or error text.

sections.title: The organization library: Not in this version
The organization library: Routes
sections.text:
These routes use admin scope, like import.
| Route | Answer |
 
| `GET /api/org-library` | `{organization, packages: [entry + blob: "ready"\|"unavailable"\|"unsupported" + installed], installs}`. `{organization: null, packages: []}` with no organization. |
| `GET /api/org-library/packages/:packageId` | `{package, document}`: the preview, read from the checked file. |
| `POST /api/org-library/add {packageId}` | `201` with the added records · `200 {alreadyAdded: true}` · `404` not listed or switched off · `409 newer_app_required` · `503 blob_unavailable` · `422 invalid_package` |
| `GET /api/org-library/skills?botId=` | Offered skills of added packages, with `added` per bot. |
| `POST /api/org-library/skills {botId, installId, name}` | `201 {skill}`: puts one offered skill on a bot, switched on. |
Fixtures have no Electron parent. For tests, `POST /api/testing/org-library
{library}` relays a catalog instead. The route exists only when the server
starts with `SAGAX_TEST_ORG_LIBRARY_KEY`, and the request carries that key in
`x-openmausbot-test-org-library`. Production never sets the key.

sections.title: The organization library
sections.text:
An organization's Admin can share packages (whole teams, or skills on their
own) with the desktops that belong to it, and with its Customers. In
Sagax they appear under Templates → From {Organization}, the first
tab. One click on Add adds a package. There is no confirmation step,
because the person's click is the decision. Details opens the same
preview a shared file gets.
With no organization account nothing changes: the tab is absent, every
route below answers `{organization: null}`, no file is written and nothing
is reported.

sections.title: The organization library: What Add does
sections.text:
The package goes through the same importer as a file (`server/package-import.ts`),
called with `trust: "org"` from `server/org-library.ts` and nowhere else.
Compared with a file:
- Skills arrive switched on. The organization's Admin published them,
 so Admin was the review. Their source reads `org: / @ `,
 and the file's own `source` is ignored.
- Routines still arrive paused. Bots still start on Ask, with no
 connected-app access and the installation's default model. Connections
 are still created switched off, without values.
- Every record is stamped with its install. A bot's wire-visible
 `installedPackage` gains `source: "org"`, `installId`, `publisher`, `ref`
 and `sha256`. Server-side only, each record also keeps two hashes for
 every part: `r`, the part as released, and `w`, the part as written here.
 The hashes live on bots (`packageBase`), group chats (`installedPackage`),
 routines (`installedPackage`) and skill state (`package`). The later
 automatic update uses them to tell your edits from the publisher's changes.
 Value shapes are in `server/package-parts.ts`.
- A skills-only package creates no records. Its skills are *offered*:
 Bot → Skills → From {Organization} lists them, and Add there puts
 one on that bot, switched on and stamped. A team's skills that no bot
 uses are offered the same way. Offered skills are read from the release
 file that was added. Electron removes a release file a week after the
 catalog stops naming it, and then those skills are no longer offered,
 though skills already on a bot stay.
- Adding twice does nothing. The install id is derived from the Admin
 address, the organization and the package, so the same package is the
 same install on every reconnect. A second Add answers `200
 {alreadyAdded: true}`.
A bot added from the organization's library shows where it came from in
Bot settings → Identity: "From Sales desk 1.3.0 · Acme Partners". A bot
imported from a file shows no such line, as before. This version never
changes something it already added. When the catalog names a newer release,
the card says "Version X available. Updates arrive automatically in an
upcoming Sagax update."
Required is treated as Available in this version, with a "Recommended
by …" badge. Entries the organization switched off are hidden, and
their copies stay.

sections.title: The organization library: Withdrawn releases
sections.text:
When the catalog lists an added release under `withdrawnReleases`, its
skills are switched off (on its own bots, where an offered skill was added,
and on bots someone made from its presets), its routines are paused, its
presets leave New bot, the install is marked withdrawn, and the bot's
provenance line adds "Withdrawn by ".
This happens once, on the change. If you switch something back on
afterwards, it stays on. A team you already removed stays removed, but an
offered skill it left on another bot is switched off the same way, once. A
package that disappears from the catalog changes nothing: copies stay.

sections.title: Organization member API (`/api/org/member/*`)
sections.text:
What a person may do with their own Sagax bots from an AI client attached to
Perspicax (Claude Code, claude.ai, Cursor, any MCP client), under their own
identity. Perspicax serves it as its `sagax_*` tools. Plan: Perspicax
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-09-master-implementation-plan.md`, lot C.1.
Code: `server/org-member-routes.ts`, wired in `server/index.ts`
(`createOrgMemberRoutes`, `performAsMember`).

sections.title: Organization member API (`/api/org/member/*`): Permissions
sections.text:
| Key | Member default | What |
 
| `clients.botsRead` | on | list their bots, read their conversations, and read rules, documents, memory and connector names of bots they own |
| `clients.botsMessage` | on | send a message and wait for the answer |
| `clients.routinesRun` | on (always) | run a routine now, read a run |
| `clients.routinesRead` | on (always) | list their own routines and read one routine's full instructions |
| `clients.routinesWrite` | on (always) | enable, disable, rename, and edit schedule or instructions of routines they own |
| `clients.approvalsAnswer` | off (the bot's owner holds it for their own bots) | allow or deny a card |
| `clients.peopleNudge` | off | nudge a person |
| `clients.agentsCreate` | off | create a temporary agent with `agents/create_agent`, delete one with `agents/delete_agent` |
Keys have two segments (`group.name`): Perspicax refuses a catalogue with
any other shape, so the plan's `clients.bots.read` is written
`clients.botsRead`.

sections.title: Organization member API (`/api/org/member/*`): Routes
sections.text:
| Method and path | Permission | What |
 
| `GET capabilities` | none | the version and the routes |
| `GET bots` | `clients.botsRead` | the bots the person can see, with status |
| `POST bots/{id}/messages` | `clients.botsMessage` | send, optionally wait up to 120 s |
| `GET threads/{id}?since&limit` | `clients.botsRead` | messages since a cursor, steps, pending cards |
| `GET threads/{id}/stream?anchor&wait` | `clients.botsRead` | watch a running turn, streamed (lot C.3) |
| `GET routines` | `clients.routinesRead` | the person's own routines |
| `GET routines/{id}` | `clients.routinesRead` | one routine, full instructions |
| `PATCH routines/{id}` | `clients.routinesWrite` | enable/disable, rename, edit schedule or instructions |
| `POST routines/{id}/run` | `clients.routinesRun` | run now |
| `GET routines/runs/{id}` | `clients.routinesRun` | one run |
| `GET bots/{id}/rules` | `clients.botsRead` | rules of a bot the person owns |
| `GET bots/{id}/docs` | `clients.botsRead` | documents of a bot the person owns |
| `GET bots/{id}/memory` | `clients.botsRead` | memory of a bot the person owns |
| `GET bots/{id}/connectors` | `clients.botsRead` | connector names of a bot the person owns |
| `GET approvals?status=pending` | `clients.botsRead` | the cards waiting on the person, across their conversations (2026-10-17) |
| `GET approvals/{id}?threadId` | `clients.botsRead` | may the person answer this card (lot C.3) |
| `POST approvals/{id}` | `clients.approvalsAnswer`, or owning the bot | allow, deny or pick an option |
| `POST people/{id}/nudge` | `clients.peopleNudge` | nudge |
| `POST agents/{tool}` | per tool (below) | the agent-to-agent tools |
### `GET capabilities`
 `{ "api": 1, "version": "0.4.16", "routes": ["GET bots", "GET capabilities", "POST bots/{id}/messages"] }` 
### `GET bots`
- `source`: `mine`, `shared` (shared with them or their team) or
 `organization` (published to the organization's Browse Bots).
- `status`: `idle`, `working`, `waiting` (a card waits for someone) or
 `archived`, for the person's own conversations.
- `canMessage`: the person can use the bot. A published bot they cannot use
 is listed with `false`: they can copy it in Sagax.
- `threadId`: the person's own conversation with the bot.
- `owner.sub` is filled for the person's own bots only.
### `POST bots/{id}/messages`
 `{ "text": "Count the open tickets of Acme", "wait": 60 }` 
- `text`: 1 to 32,000 characters. Sent as the person, in their own
 conversation with the bot (Sagax's rule on an organization server).
- `threadId`: one of their conversations with this bot; `newThread: true`
 starts a new one instead (not both).
- Without `threadId`, an AI client (any actor but the Sagax console) writes
 in its own hidden conversation with the bot (#291): the newest one it
 opened, or a new one. A hidden conversation belongs to the person and stays
 reachable (the bot's Activity panel, a link, `GET threads/{id}`), but it is

sections.title: Organization member API (`/api/org/member/*`): The gate
sections.text:
- Answered before the session gate and before loopback trust, like the
 admin API (`docs/org-admin-api.md`). The only credential is an assertion
 Perspicax signs per request (`Authorization: Bearer `): the
 console assertion's format (`typ` `pulsabot-console+jwt`, ES256, `aud` this
 server's public origin, at most 120 s, single use `jti`, `server_id` equal
 to the link's, `role`, `teams`), with `act.sub` `perspicax-mcp` (an AI
 client) or `console`. The admin API keeps accepting `console` only: an AI
 client's assertion is refused there (`401 assertion_invalid`).
- The person is the assertion's `sub`. They must be known here (the
 directory lists them), active in Perspicax and not turned off in Sagax:
 else `403 unknown_person` or `403 person_disabled`. A person does not
 need to have signed in to Sagax.
- An admin is an organization admin both in the assertion (`role: admin`)
 and on this server.
- Each route needs one permission of the catalogue (`shared/permissions.ts`,
 group `clients`). Without it: `403 forbidden_permission` with
 `permission` naming the key. An admin holds every key.
- The route then performs the matching Sagax route as the person,
 through a 60 s session of theirs (`SessionRegistry.actAs`, memory only, not
 listed, not renewed, revoked after the call). Every rule the person meets
 in Sagax holds unchanged: which bots they see, private threads, who may
 answer a card, who may Run now. A refusal of that route passes through
 with its status, its sentence and its `permission` when it names one.
- A refusal is `{code, message, reason, error}` like the admin API. Every
 answer carries `X-Sagax-Member-Api: 1` and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Every write leaves one row of the admin activity log, category `client`,
 actor `{kind: "person", principalId, via: "perspicax-mcp"}` (`console`
 when the console signed it). No row carries a message text.

sections.title: Organization branding
sections.text:
An organization administrator can upload a logo and up to 24 shared bot icons
in Admin → Branding. Use PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 5 MB per upload. Admin resizes
the images before saving; the normalized collection is limited to 128 KiB.
Members connect through Settings → Organization as usual. The logo appears
in the sidebar and Organization settings. Shared icons appear in each bot's
avatar customization alongside the normal upload and mascot options.
Connected desktop apps refresh branding on the existing session heartbeat.
Use Refresh in Organization settings to fetch changes immediately. Older
Admins return no branding, so the standard app appearance remains unchanged.
Personal users do not need to sign in.
Selecting a shared icon stores a copy as a normal local avatar attachment.
It remains with that bot, including in workspace backups, even if an admin
later removes the icon or the member disconnects. Disconnecting hides the
organization logo and shared library; it does not delete personal avatars.
Branding does not change the installed application name, Dock/Start-menu icon,
model permissions, or authentication. Remote workspace pages cannot read the
local desktop's organization branding.

sections.title: Install the phone web app
sections.text:
The browser UI can be added to your phone's Home Screen. It opens in its own
window and uses the same workspace, conversations and pairing as the browser.
1. Open your workspace's HTTPS web link in Safari on iPhone or Chrome on
 Android. Use an existing hosted address, Tailscale HTTPS address or your own
 HTTPS reverse proxy. A phone cannot reach the computer through a localhost
 link. See self-hosting for remote access and pairing.
2. Pair the browser with that workspace using its normal pairing flow.
3. On iPhone, open Safari's Share menu, choose Add to Home Screen, keep
 Open as Web App enabled if Safari offers it, then tap Add. On Android,
 open Chrome's menu and choose Install app or Add to Home screen.
4. Open Sagax from the Home Screen. If that browser keeps Home Screen
 apps in separate storage, pair this new window too. Installation does not
 grant access to a workspace by itself.
The installed start address is the workspace root; pairing codes and URL tokens
are not saved in the manifest. Use a new pairing invitation if access expires
or the device is revoked.
Your server must be running and reachable. This web app does not add offline
chat, push notifications or native phone computer control.

sections.title: PR evidence media: Orphan media (issue #1386)
sections.text:
Media under `docs/` that no tracked file referenced were removed from the
index and left on disk under `pr-assets/` when the move ran. Git history still
holds the blobs; they are simply no longer part of the tree going forward.
To find new orphans later:
 
Do not put third-party app captures or real personal install data (hostnames,
names, emails) into the repo. Committed captures must come from galleries or
fixtures with synthetic data only.

sections.title: PR evidence media
sections.text:
Visual proof for pull requests (before/after screenshots, short clips, GIFs)
does not live under tracked `docs/` unless a tracked file cites that media by
path or by a specific directory name.

sections.title: PR evidence media: Related
sections.text:
- UI screenshot expectation: CONTRIBUTING.md
- Verification captures that stay in-tree when cited:
 verification/README.md

sections.title: PR evidence media: Where PR evidence lives
sections.text:
- In the PR body: attach images or short videos on the GitHub pull request
 itself. Prefer MP4 or WebP over large GIFs.
- Local `pr-assets/` (gitignored): optional working copy on a developer
 machine for drafts and comparisons. The folder mirrors former `docs/`
 relative paths (for example `pr-assets/screenshots/composer-one-line.gif`).
 It is never committed.
- Tracked `docs/screenshots/` and `docs/verification/`: only media that a
 tracked file still references (a markdown path, a capture script, AGENTS
 notes, a plan). Keep those; they document shipped behavior.

sections.title: Preset bots: HTTP
sections.text:
All admin scope.
- `GET /api/bot-presets` → `{presets: [{id, source: "file"|"org", key, name,
 description?, packageName, release, publisherName?, bot, skills: [{name,
 description}], skillsEnabled, playbooks, notes}]}`.
- `DELETE /api/bot-presets/:id` removes an imported preset; an organization's
 answers `409`.
- `POST /api/bots` with `preset: " "` adds the preset's playbooks, skills
 and starter notes to the new bot and stamps it. Name, look and instructions
 are the request's own fields, as for any bot.
- `POST /api/teams/export` with `includeDefaultsPreset: true` (and optionally
 `presetName`, `presetDescription`, `presetAvatar` as a data URL) adds the
 New bot defaults preset to a team file. With `kind: "library"` instead of
 `team`, it saves a preset file (`name`, `release`, `notes`, `includeMemory`,
 `dryRun` as for a team).
- `POST /api/teams/import` adds a preset file's presets and answers
 `{presets: [{id, key, name}], offeredSkills, bots: [], section: ""}`.
 `POST /api/org-library/add` answers with the same `presets` list, and the
 install's entry in `org-library/state.json` records them under `presets`
 (`{ : {presetId, r}}`, `r` the release-side hash of contract §1.6).
See verification/presets.md for how this is tested.

sections.title: Preset bots
sections.text:
A preset is a named starting point in New bot. Choosing one fills in the
new bot's name, title, description, standing instructions and look, and when
you press Create bot it also brings the preset's skills, playbooks and
starter notes. You can change every field before creating the bot.
Presets come from a shared file (a team file or a preset file someone sent
you) or from your organization's shelf (Templates → From {Organization},
see org-library.md). In New bot's Starting role list,
your organization's presets come first under From {Organization}, then
Imported presets, then the built-in roles.

sections.title: Preset bots: Sharing presets
sections.text:
Two ways, both saving the same file format (team-sharing.md):
- With a team. In Share team…, tick Include my New bot defaults as
 a preset. It is off unless you tick it: your New bot defaults are yours
 until you share them. The team's Include starter notes box also decides
 whether the preset's notes go in.
- On their own. Settings → General → Defaults for new bots → Share as
 preset… saves a preset file: the preset and its skills, no team, no bots.
 Choose the preset's name, a description, the version and whether to include
 the picture and starter notes.
Either way the preset is made from your saved New bot defaults through the
allowlist above, and every text part passes through the same secret redaction
as a team file. The dialog lists what was removed or left out. There is no
confirmation step: Save file is the decision.
A preset file is added in Templates → Import like a team file. The
preview shows the preset bots and any skills the file only offers; Add
presets puts the presets in New bot and changes nothing else. A file with
skills but no bots or presets has nothing to add here and is refused with a
sentence. Adding the same file twice offers its presets once.

sections.title: Preset bots: What a preset holds
Preset bots: Where it came from decides the skills
sections.text:
- From a file: the preset's skills are added switched off, like every
 skill in a shared file. Switch them on in the bot's Skills settings after
 reading them.
- From your organization: the skills are added switched on, because
 your organization's Admin published them. Each also carries the install's
 skill stamp (contract §3.2: the install, the skill's name, the release, and
 the `SKILL.md` hashes as released and as written), marked `via: "preset"`,
 so a later automatic update can tell your own edits from the publisher's
 changes. The bot is still yours, not part of the package: it never keeps
 the package added, so a team you deleted can be added again.
The New bot dialog says which applies before you create the bot. A preset's
skills and starter notes win over your New bot defaults' own skill or note of
the same name. The bot records where it came from (`installedPackage` with
`presetKey`).
A preset from an organization release that was withdrawn, or from a team you
deleted, is no longer offered, and a bot already made from a withdrawn one
has that release's skills switched off (once; switching them back on is
yours). Which presets are offered follows the organization library's own
state (`OrgLibrary.installStatuses()` in `server/org-library.ts`), not a
separate read of `state.json`, so New bot and the shelf never disagree. With
no organization there are no installs and nothing is hidden. Adding the same organization package again, for example a
team you deleted, refreshes its presets in place rather than adding copies. Organization presets are
managed in Admin; an imported preset can be removed with Remove from New
bot under the Starting role list (no confirmation step).

sections.title: Preset bots: Where presets are kept
sections.text:
`org-library/presets.json` in the data folder: one row per preset (where it
came from, which install it belongs to, the package name and version, and the
preset exactly as the file carried it), plus the skill and playbook
definitions those presets use, so a bot can be made from a preset after the
file or the organization's release is gone. What this installation last
shared as a preset file (its package id and version) is kept in
`published-library.json`, so the next share suggests the next version.

sections.title: Démarrage rapide MSP (10 minutes): Avant de commencer
sections.text:
- Un abonnement à au moins un moteur que vous payez déjà (par exemple Claude
 ou Grok). Sagax ne revend pas de modèle : vous vous connectez avec votre
 propre abonnement.
- Sagax sur votre ordinateur (voir ci-dessous).

sections.title: Démarrage rapide MSP (10 minutes)
sections.text:
Ce guide mène un nouveau MSP de zéro à un premier résultat concret avec
Pulsatrix Sagax et Pulsatrix Perspicax. Comptez une dizaine de minutes, à
faire, pas seulement à lire.
Sagax est l'application où une personne parle à ses bots : chaque bot tourne
sur un vrai moteur d'IA (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, etc.) avec son nom, son
modèle et sa mémoire. Perspicax est la passerelle où un administrateur branche
les outils du MSP (un connecteur PSA, un outil de sécurité, un outil de
sauvegarde) et les sert aux bots. Ce guide couvre la part Sagax ; la part
Perspicax (ajouter un produit, appel guidé en lecture seule) est dans le guide
jumeau du dépôt Perspicax, `docs/quickstart-msp.md`.

sections.title: Démarrage rapide MSP (10 minutes): English
sections.text:
This guide takes a brand-new MSP from zero to a first real result with
Pulsatrix Sagax and Pulsatrix Perspicax. Budget about ten minutes, to do, not
just to read.
Sagax is the app where a person talks to their bots: each bot runs on a real AI
engine (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, and others) with its own name, model and
memory. Perspicax is the gateway where an administrator connects the MSP's
tools (a PSA connector, a security tool, a backup tool) and serves them to
bots. This guide covers the Sagax part; the Perspicax part (add a product, the
guided read-only first call) is in the twin guide in the Perspicax repo,
`docs/quickstart-msp.md`.
### The 10-minute path
1. Install and open Sagax.
2. Connect an engine (the model provider you already pay for).
3. Create your first bot, on Auto.
4. Send a first message, then ask the bot one safe read action.
### Before you start
- A subscription to at least one engine you already pay for (for example Claude
 or Grok). Sagax does not resell models: you sign in with your own
 subscription.
- Sagax on your computer (see below).
### Step 1: install and open Sagax
Download Sagax from the repo's Download section:
- macOS: open the `.dmg` (Apple Silicon `arm64` or Intel `x64`) and drag
 Sagax into Applications. Signed and notarized by Apple.
- Windows (x64 and arm64, one installer): run the `-setup.exe`. Signed
 from 0.8.3; if SmartScreen still warns, choose More info, then Run anyway.
On first launch, a guided First run walks the three real steps below. It is
dismissible: a Later button and Escape close it, and it does not come back
next launch. Steps already done are skipped.
### Step 2: connect an engine
The Your model providers screen shows the engines found on this computer,
ready or to set up. Click Connect an engine and follow the chosen engine's
connect flow. An engine already connected is marked done and the step is
skipped.
### Step 3: create your first bot (on Auto)
On the Create your first bot screen, click Create my first bot. The bot
is created with the engine and model on Auto: nothing to choose to get
started, and its approval level stays on Approve for me. You can set the
engine, model and level later; More options opens the full dialog for the
advanced case.
### Step 4: send your first message
On the Send your first message screen, the guide closes onto the new bot's
chat, with the caret already in the composer. Write your first message and
press Enter.
For an MSP, ask one safe read action, for example "list the open tickets". The
PSA and other product tools come from Perspicax, served to the bot through
profiles: see the Perspicax guide, `docs/quickstart-msp.md`, to connect a
product and confirm it answers with the guided read-only first call. The link
between a Sagax server and Perspicax is described, on the Perspicax side, in
`docs/sagax.md`.
### The approval model, in brief
- A read-only call never raises an approval card: the bot reads and answers.

sections.title: Démarrage rapide MSP (10 minutes): Étape 1 : installer et ouvrir Sagax
sections.text:
Téléchargez Sagax depuis la page Download du dépôt :
- macOS : ouvrez le `.dmg` (Apple Silicon `arm64` ou Intel `x64`) et
 glissez Sagax dans Applications. Signée et notariée par Apple.
- Windows (x64 et arm64, un seul programme d'installation) : lancez le
 `-setup.exe`. Signé depuis la 0.8.3 ; si SmartScreen avertit quand même,
 choisissez Informations complémentaires, puis Exécuter quand même.
Au premier lancement, un Premier démarrage guidé enchaîne les trois vraies
étapes ci-dessous. Il est refermable : un bouton Plus tard et la touche
Échap le ferment, et il ne revient pas au prochain lancement. Les étapes déjà
faites sont sautées.

sections.title: Démarrage rapide MSP (10 minutes): Étape 2 : connecter un moteur
sections.text:
L'écran Vos fournisseurs de modèles montre les moteurs trouvés sur cet
ordinateur, prêts ou à configurer. Cliquez sur Connecter un moteur et
suivez la connexion du moteur choisi. Un moteur déjà connecté est marqué comme
fait et l'étape est sautée.

sections.title: Démarrage rapide MSP (10 minutes): Étape 3 : créer son premier bot (sur Auto)
sections.text:
À l'écran Créez votre premier bot, cliquez sur Créer mon premier bot.
Le bot se crée avec le moteur et le modèle sur Auto : rien à choisir pour
commencer, et son niveau d'autorisation reste sur Approuver à ma place.
Vous pourrez préciser le moteur, le modèle et le niveau plus tard ; le bouton
Plus d'options ouvre le dialogue complet pour le cas avancé.

sections.title: Démarrage rapide MSP (10 minutes): Étape 4 : envoyer son premier message
sections.text:
À l'écran Envoyez votre premier message, le guide se referme sur la
conversation du nouveau bot, le curseur déjà dans la zone de saisie. Écrivez
votre premier message et appuyez sur Entrée.
Pour un MSP, demandez une seule action sûre en lecture, par exemple « liste les
billets ouverts ». Les outils du PSA et des autres produits viennent de
Perspicax, servis au bot par profil : voir le guide Perspicax,
`docs/quickstart-msp.md`, pour brancher un produit et confirmer qu'il répond
avec l'appel guidé en lecture seule. Le lien entre un serveur Sagax et
Perspicax est décrit, côté Perspicax, dans `docs/sagax.md`.

sections.title: Démarrage rapide MSP (10 minutes): Le chemin en 10 minutes
sections.text:
1. Installer et ouvrir Sagax.
2. Connecter un moteur (le fournisseur de modèles que vous payez déjà).
3. Créer son premier bot, sur Auto.
4. Envoyer un premier message, puis demander au bot une seule action sûre en
 lecture.
Les étapes 1 à 4 sont détaillées ici. Pour brancher un outil du MSP et le
servir au bot, voir le guide Perspicax.

sections.title: Démarrage rapide MSP (10 minutes): Le modèle d'approbation, en bref
sections.text:
- Une lecture seule ne déclenche jamais de carte d'approbation : le bot lit et
 répond.
- Une écriture, un envoi, un paiement ou le contact d'une vraie personne attend
 un oui : une carte par oui, avec essai à blanc.
- Le niveau par défaut d'un nouveau bot est Approuver à ma place. Vous le
 changez par bot, et vous pouvez écrire des règles en clair. Détails dans
 `docs/approval-levels.md`.
Bon démarrage.

sections.title: Reach me ("Me joindre"): Channels
sections.text:
| Channel | What it needs | How you answer |
 
| Phone notifications | The Sagax app paired on your iPhone or Android phone | In the app, or Allow/Deny on the banner (iPhone) |
| Text message | Your Perspicax Voice line, and your own number verified on it | Text back the code, then `oui`/`non` (or your answer) |
| Microsoft Teams | A bot of yours whose engine has a Teams connector (Microsoft 365 on claude.ai, Microsoft Teams on grok.com) | Write the code and your answer in your own Teams chat with yourself, within 40 minutes |
| Telegram | Your own Telegram bot, made with BotFather | Reply to it with the code and your answer |
| WhatsApp | Your own WhatsApp Business number (WhatsApp Cloud API, your Meta app) | Reply with the code and your answer |
Every message carries a short code for that card only, for example
`KM3X`. Answer `KM3X oui` to allow, `KM3X non` to deny, or `KM3X` followed
by your answer to a question. A reply without the right code, from another
number or another chat, answers nothing. A card that needs your security key
can only be denied from outside: open Sagax to allow it. A card of a
confidential conversation never shows its content outside the app.

sections.title: Reach me ("Me joindre"): Hours
sections.text:
"Any time", or one or more ranges of days and times in your time zone
(22:00 to 07:00 runs past midnight). Outside them nothing leaves the app for
that bot; a card still open when your next range starts is sent then.

sections.title: Reach me ("Me joindre")
sections.text:
When a bot has a question or an approval that waits on you, it can reach you
outside the app. You choose how, and when, for each bot: Bot panel >
Overview > Reach me. Nobody else chooses for you and no administrator has to
turn it on. Your Primary Bot can change it for you from any conversation
(`sagax_settings`, keys `notifications.reachMe`,
`notifications.reachMeTelegram` and `notifications.reachMeWhatsApp`).

sections.title: Reach me ("Me joindre"): Teams
sections.text:
Sagax has no Teams app of its own. Each message, and each check for your
answer, is a short run of one of your own bots ("Reach me (Teams)" in
Automations), with your own engine sign-in. That one send to your own chat
asks for no extra approval; anything else the run tries keeps its usual card.
Sagax looks for your answer 2, 6, 15 and 40 minutes after the message.

sections.title: Reach me ("Me joindre"): Telegram
sections.text:
1. In Telegram, ask BotFather for a new bot and copy its token.
2. On the bot page, turn Telegram on, paste the token, Connect.
3. Open the link Sagax shows and press Start. That chat is now the only one
 your bot listens to.
The token is sealed on the server and never shown again. Disconnect forgets
it and the chat.

sections.title: Reach me ("Me joindre"): Text messages
sections.text:
Texts go from your Perspicax Voice line to your own number, only when the
line lists that number as verified. Each text is billed by the telephony
provider: Sagax never retries one and never answers your reply by text.
The reply reaches Sagax through the Perspicax Voice inbound route
(`POST /api/org/telephony/inbound`), which hands it to `reachMeSmsReply`
(`server/reach-me/inbound.ts`) before the bot's phone triggers.
Developer notes: `AGENTS.md`, "Reach me: one setting per bot to reach the
person outside the app".

sections.title: Reach me ("Me joindre"): WhatsApp
sections.text:
1. In your Meta app (WhatsApp > API Setup), copy an access token and your
 business number's Phone Number ID. For replies, copy the app secret too
 (App settings > Basic).
2. On the bot page, turn WhatsApp on, paste them, Connect. Sagax checks them
 with Meta and shows the business number.
3. Prove your own number: open the WhatsApp link and send `SAGAX `,
 or type your number and get the code by your message template, then type
 it back. Only that number is written to or read from.
4. For replies, in your Meta app (WhatsApp > Configuration), paste the
 callback URL and the verify token (Copy buttons on the bot page) and
 subscribe to `messages`. This needs the server's public webhook address
 (`SAGAX_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_URL`); without one, WhatsApp only notifies you and
 you answer in Sagax.
WhatsApp lets a business write plain text only within 24 hours of your last
message. Outside that window Sagax uses your approved message template: set
its name and language, and your WhatsApp Business Account ID (WhatsApp >
API Setup), on the bot page; it needs one body parameter, which carries the
card's text. Sagax reads that template at Meta (a free read that sends
nothing) each time you save it, and again when Meta refuses a message for
its template. Until Meta says it is approved, in that language, with that
one parameter, WhatsApp shows as not ready, with the reason and what to do
(Check again on the page). Every message is billed by Meta to your account:
Sagax never retries one. The token and app secret are sealed on the server
and never shown again. Disconnect forgets them and your number.

sections.title: Remote Sessions page and unattended access (Sagax control plane): Code signing
sections.text:
- Windows: the service binary must be Authenticode signed.
- macOS: the LaunchDaemon binary must be signed and notarized.
- Linux: no OS signing requirement; distribute from a trusted package.
- An unsigned agent is flagged on the page (the Unattended column shows "Agent
 not code signed"). Ship signed builds for unattended.

sections.title: Remote Sessions page and unattended access (Sagax control plane): Enrolled hosts (2026-10-26)
sections.text:
The contract is `docs/inscription-hote.md` in `sagax-remote-access` ("Côté
Sagax"). Perspicax is the authority: it keeps the enrolled hosts
(`remote_support_hosts`), keyed by `host_id` (`h_` and 32 hex, the fingerprint
of the host's own key, never a hostname or a serial: E3).
- The page shows an "Enrolled hosts" section above the sessions
 (`src/components/remote-session/UnattendedHostsSection.tsx`): the readable
 name, the organization when it is a name, the scope, enrolled, expires, last
 seen and the state (enrolled, expired, revoked). The `host_id` is only in the
 name's tooltip and behind the Copy button, never in the text.
- "Unattended access" (`POST /api/admin/remote-sessions/hosts/ /open`)
 shows on an enrolled host. Any person
 who reaches this server may open (no admin approval, decision 2026-10-26).
 Sagax makes a client key for that session only (as for a coded open), sends
 `remote_support_open` with `host_id` and the public nodekey, follows
 `remote_support_status` until the host picks the session at its beat, and
 the usual registrar posts the card and the panel row (`client = "app"`) in
 the conversation of the person's Primary Bot (else another bot of theirs
 with a Perspicax profile). The page then opens the live control overlay by
 itself.
- "Revoke" (`POST /api/admin/remote-sessions/hosts/ /revoke`, optional
 body `{ reason }`) shows on every host not yet revoked, flag OFF included
 (M2), with a confirm and an optional reason. Who may: the person who
 enrolled the host revokes it themselves (their own environment, no admin),
 and an admin revokes any host of the organization; Perspicax decides and
 Sagax adds no gate of its own. Sessions opened from this page on that host
 end here at once; Perspicax ends the others and the host stops and
 uninstalls at its next beat (a 410: only a 410 makes the host uninstall; a
 404, a 5xx or a network failure is retried with backoff).
- Every open writes an `unattended.open` line and every revoke a
 `remote_host.revoked` line (the name Perspicax gives the same act) in
 `remote-session-actions.jsonl`: the actor is the person who acted (M4), the
 host is in its own field, with the reason and the UTC time (`atUtc`). The
 legacy consent revoke writes the same kind; it is open to the person who
 recorded the consent and to an admin.
- Server: `server/remote-unattended-hosts.ts` (list, open, revoke),
 `shared/remote-unattended-host.ts` (rows, states, what may be opened),
 `openUnattendedSession` in `server/remote-support-local.ts`.
Perspicax tools (names frozen with Perspicax): `remote_support_hosts` (answer
`{ hosts: [{ host_id, hostname, org, scope, created_at, expires_at,
last_seen_at, revoked_at, ... }] }`), `remote_support_host_revoke`
(`{ host_id, reason? }`) and `remote_support_open` with `host_id`, which
answers the session's `code`, as status and close stay keyed by code. A
server without them reads as "list not available".

sections.title: Remote Sessions page and unattended access (Sagax control plane): Flow skill wording (to mirror into the Flow skill)
sections.text:
> Enabling unattended access on a client host is done with the end user present
> and the client organization consenting. Install the "Sagax Remote Control"
> service from the Pulsatrix Assist helper or the CLI
> (`pulsatrix-assist install --unattended --org --code 
> --consent-recorded-by `), record who consented, and set the banner and
> tray options per the client's policy. The install is auditable and the host
> shows the service by name. To stop it, uninstall locally or revoke from the
> Sagax Remote Sessions page; revoke cuts any live session.

sections.title: Remote Sessions page and unattended access (Sagax control plane): Host-side follow-ups (pulsatrix-assist)
sections.text:
From the security review of PR #981. Sagax no longer gates these behind a
server flag (2026-11-01); they still need to land in the helper:
