sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: Desktop permissions
sections.text:
- macOS: `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` (electron-builder.yml) and the
 `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` entitlement
 (build/entitlements.mac.plist) are in the signed build; macOS asks once.
- Windows: Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone must allow desktop
 apps. No macOS helper is involved.
- Electron grants the microphone to the local UI and, in server mode, to the
 organization server's origin drawn with the bundled UI, audio only
 (`electron/app-permissions.mjs`, `microphoneOrigins`).

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: Full-duplex conversation (issue #292)
sections.text:
The stacked answers the maintainer heard were not the TTS sentence queue (that is
one reply's clauses, cancelled on barge-in). They were the harness
steer queue: talking while the bot was thinking did not interrupt
(`call-machine.ts`), a send that raced `stoppingThreads` was
`queueSteeredMessage`, and drain played each leftover utterance as
the next answer.
`CallSettings.fullDuplex` (device-local, `omb.voiceCall.v1`, default
off on every channel; rev 3 drops the on that 0.5.x stored) plus
`voiceCall.duplex` on the send, and only while `SAGAX_VOICE_FULL_DUPLEX=1`:
confirmed speech while the bot is busy or speaking cancels that turn; the
server never steers or queues those words. The thinking cue is 400 ms
instead of 1200 ms so
the line is not dead air. Approvals stay spoken yes or no and are not
cancelled. Tools still run on the bot. A "stop" is a stop only when it is
the whole utterance ("stop", "arrête", "arrête ça", "ok stop", "stop
please", with at most two filler or polite words around it,
`voice-topics.ts` `isStopUtterance`): "Stop le service AcmeGuard sur
SRV-01" is work for the bot, sent like any other request, never swallowed.
The call speaks no canned filler
and no tool-chip narration; the prompt asks the bot to say so once, in
its own words, only when something will genuinely take a while. What the
call does say on its own while the bot works in silence is a progress
line built from the turn's real tool events (see "Progress lines" below). A duplex
send that races another is latest-wins (the slower one is superseded, never queued).
`startTurn` thread_busy is retried until the interrupt cap. Cancelled
turns stop streaming (`content.delta` of that turnId is not broadcast).
The client speech fence (`speech-fence.ts`, iOS `CallConversation`)
keeps `dropOldReply` across the send, so a dying answer that lands
after the new user line is marked interrupted and never spoken.
xAI Speech-to-Speech (`wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime`, grok-voice-latest)
is still not the brain: it would drop Sagax tools, memory, approvals
and MCP. Tests: `src/lib/voice-mode/duplex-policy.test.ts`,
`speech-fence.test.ts`, `call-logic.test.ts`,
`server/voice-call-duplex.test.ts`,
`scripts/voice-duplex-harness.test.ts`,
`server/voice-call-reliability.e2e.test.ts` (duplex case).
Each utterance has an `utteranceId` (also its `sendId`): the server
delivers it once, and answers a second send of it with the first receipt.
Words steered into a running turn are counted as received once the engine
says a model call took them in (Claude's `--replay-user-messages` echo,
`steer.received`), so the next turn never offers them again as a message
"you may already have".
On a barge-in the player reports what played by its audio clock: the
sentences heard, the share of the one cut (at a word), and the rest, plus
what the bot wrote but had not yet handed to the voice. The turn that cut
the bot carries `voiceCall.heard` and `voiceCall.unheard`; the bot reads
"They heard up to: '...'.

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: Latency
sections.text:
The pause the person hears is measured stage by stage for every call turn,
under the turn's `utteranceId` (ids and milliseconds, never the words):
- The page (`src/lib/voice-mode/latency.ts`): `endpoint` (last voiced frame
 to the detector's end of turn), `stt` (to the words), `dispatch` (to the
 send), `firstToken` (to the answer's first streamed text), `firstSentence`
 (to a speakable clause), `tts` (to its first audio bytes), `playback` (to
 audible), and `total`. With `localStorage["omb.voiceCall.debug"]` set to
 `"1"` the console logs a `[voice-latency]` line per turn and the call's
 settings card shows the last answer's stages.
- The server (`server/voice-latency.ts`) logs, under the same id,
 `received->dispatch`, `dispatch->engine` (warm, or cold start) and
 `engine->first-token`. A Claude relaunch logs which spawn contract fields
 changed (names only, `server/drivers/spawn-contract.ts`). A Grok turn is
 "warm" when it prompts the live native session as is (no handshake, no
 `session/load`).
What keeps it short:
- A warm engine for the whole call. Every turn used to relaunch the
 Claude CLI (the agents proxy's per-turn comms token was part of the spawn
 contract): a 2.5 to 3 s cold start on each answer (process boot, MCP
 servers, the session read back; measured from native logs). While the
 thread is on a call the turn carries `keepWarm`: the token rides a 0600
 per-thread file (`SAGAX_COMMS_TOKEN_FILE`, read on each request) and
 leaves the contract. Claude starts that process when the call is accepted
 (`POST /voice/call`), before the first utterance, and the first spoken
 turn reuses it (`server/voice-call-latency.e2e.test.ts`). A hangup closes
 the idle process.
- Grok keeps one native session for the call. Grok runs over ACP: one
 pooled process per thread, whose native session is re-established
 (`session/load`, every MCP server reconnected, the history read back)
 whenever its session inputs change. The comms token was one of them, so
 every Grok call turn paid a `session/load`. On a call the token now rides
 the same token file and is masked out of the session inputs: a call turn
 is a bare `session/prompt`. Grok is also warmed when the call is
 accepted: the process pays initialize, authenticate and `session/load`
 (or `session/new` for a new conversation) with no prompt and no event in
 the thread, so the first spoken turn is a bare prompt too
 (`AcpSupport.warmSession`). What is warm, then: Claude (one process) and
 Grok (one process, one native session) for the whole call; Codex and the
 API drivers are not warmed (a Codex warm would need its handshake and
 `session/new`, not done here; API drivers cannot start without a prompt,
 and no hidden prompt is sent).
- Low reasoning effort on a call. A call turn, and the warm that starts
 its process (so both share one spawn contract), runs at the engine's low
 effort: Grok `--reasoning-effort low`, Claude `--effort low`, Codex
 `effort: low` (`server/voice-call-effort.ts`).

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: Progress lines
sections.text:
A call turn that runs tools can leave the person in silence for half a
minute. The call (desktop `LiveCall`, `src/lib/voice-mode/progress.ts`;
the Mac's older dictation call `CallView` and its room call
`GroupCallView`; iPhone `CallProgress` in `CallConversation`) then says a
short line of its own, never a canned filler: each line comes from a tool
event of this turn, the activity rows after the person's last line. None of
these desktop calls reads the server's English chip narration (the chip's
`spoken` text, which can name a tool).
- What is said: the category of the tool still running ("Je vérifie.", "I'm
 looking it up.", "Je fais la modification.", from `progressKind`: built-in
 tool names first, then the first verb of a connector tool's name), or,
 for the same work again, the number of steps finished ("3 étapes faites,
 je continue.") or "still on it". Never the tool's name, its arguments or
 an identifier (the words also go through `stripSpokenIdentifiers`).
 Tools whose own card or words are spoken (`end_call`, questions, plans)
 get none.
- Language: the call's chosen language, else (Auto) French when the
 person's last words are French and the page is in English or French,
 else the page's (`progressLocale`, `tIn`, keys `voiceMode.progress.*`). A
 language whose pack lacks the words says nothing: silence beats the wrong
 language. `CallView` and `GroupCallView` have no call language: the
 same rule with Auto. The iPhone follows the same rule
 (`CallProgress.language`), with the words of that language's
 `Localizable.xcstrings` entry, never simply the app's language.
- A room call: one turn may reach several members, so a line stays
 generic. It is said in a member's voice only when every tool row of the
 turn is that member's (`turnToolAuthor`), otherwise in the call's own
 voice, never another bot's.
- When: only in the call's thinking phase with the bot busy, nothing
 audible, nothing else queued and no approval or question waiting. The
 first line of a turn once a tool has run 1.5 s with nothing said: this is
 the quick first sentence before a slow step on every engine (Claude,
 Codex, ACP, API). Later lines need 7 s of silence (the bot's own words
 reset it) and 9 s since the last line; five a turn at most. A 500 ms tick
 asks.
- Barge-in, an interrupt or a new turn: a line being said is cut like any
 speech (it is a filler clip, never the answer's utterance and never the
 turn's first audio), and no line follows until the next turn is sent.
The model's own parallel opener (`voice.opener`, one sentence from a fast
model beside the turn) stays with HTTP Grok on a full-duplex call;
`server/voice-first-sentence.ts` says why Claude, Codex and ACP engines do
not get one.

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: Recognition reliability (2026-10-30)
sections.text:
Short answers such as names, weekdays, commands and single letters are
accepted, including non-Latin text. Only empty text, explicit hesitation
sounds and low-confidence short transcripts are discarded by the text
filter; a word's length is not evidence of noise. Desktop and iOS use the
same rule.
Each page `finalize` carries a `requestId`. For OpenAI, the provider's
`input_audio_buffer.committed` event associates its `item_id` with that
request. Partial and final transcripts retain this identity through the
server. Results can complete out of order: the page updates their own turn
and assembles probes within a turn in audio order. Only a contiguous prefix
is published; a gap or non-final segment at timeout triggers transcription
of the whole recording, rather than sending an incomplete request. Deltas
received before commit are kept by item id until the ack names their owner.
Results of a discarded,
timed-out, uploaded or reconnected turn cannot consume a newer turn's words.
xAI and older clients continue using the existing ordered chunk protocol.
This does not change the call architecture, provider preferences or duplex
defaults. Server and client changes must both be delivered for identified
OpenAI transcripts; an older server still uses ordered untagged results.
Since 2026-10-29 OpenAI and ElevenLabs can be the voice too, picked per
person and per bot, each falling back on the others (AGENTS.md, "Voice
providers"). What follows is xAI's side, unchanged.
Voice mode is the floating voice bar above the composer: the bot's name on
top, its avatar, a live waveform, then settings (Voice, Speed, Language),
transcript, mute and end. xAI does the voice; the bot stays the brain.

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: Settings
sections.text:
Voice ("Not set" is xAI's default voice), Speed (0.75x, 1x, 1.25x, 1.5x) and
Language (Auto-detect and the languages of `shared/voice-mode.ts`) live in
localStorage under `omb.voiceMode.v1`, which travels with the person on an
organization server (`shared/user-preferences.ts`). The call's own settings
(hands-free or push to talk, Only my voice, call sounds, and under
Advanced "Streaming voice" and "Faster end of turn", both on by default)
and the voiceprint
stay on the computer (`omb.voiceCall.v1`, `omb.voiceCall.voiceprint.v1`). A language xAI text to
speech does not take is spoken as `auto`; speech to text gets the base
language as a hint when xAI supports it, else it detects (Auto-detect on a
French locale: French, see Streaming speech to text).

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: Stable tools during a call
sections.text:
On an organization server each turn used to exchange the speaker's sign-in
for a fresh Perspicax MCP token per profile and revoke it after the turn; a
call's quick turns hit the rate limit and a refused exchange left the
profile out of that turn. While the thread is on a call, a turn's tokens
(and their Perspicax MCP session) are kept for the call's next turn and
reused without an exchange (`PerspicaxMcp` `keepWarm`), then revoked when
the call ends. An exchange refused for now is retried once. A call turn
whose MCP set changed is logged (`[voice-call]`), and so are the servers
added or removed when the Claude CLI relaunches.

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: The bot answers, xAI only listens and speaks
sections.text:
A call talks to the app's bot: its engine, instructions, memory, tools, MCP
servers, approvals and payer rules, with the transcript in the thread. xAI is
used only as speech to text and text to speech. Voice mode never uses xAI's
realtime voice agent, Grok responses, chat completions or function calling,
nor any mode where xAI writes the reply. Every accepted utterance becomes an
ordinary bot turn through the normal send route (attributed to the person who
spoke, private-thread rules applied), and only the bot's own reply text is
synthesized. `server/voice-call.e2e.test.ts` and `scripts/verify-voice-mode.ts`
fail if a call reaches any xAI path other than `/v1/stt`, `/v1/tts` and
`/v1/tts/voices`.

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: The bot knows it is on the phone
sections.text:
Every turn said on a call is sent with `voiceCall` (`{ callId, interrupted?,
language?, duplex? }`, stored on the person's message as `Message.voiceCall`; words
typed to a bot while its call is live carry the call id too). For such a turn
the server adds a hidden "Phone call" section to the bot's system prompt
(`server/voice-call-prompt.ts`): a live phone call with the person, words from
speech recognition that may be misheard (infer the meaning, never mention a
transcript, dictation or voice mode, never ask to type), the voice output
contract (verdict first, one to four short spoken sentences, no markdown,
lists, tables, code, emojis, URLs or file paths, never an identifier read
aloud, times and numbers said the way a person says them in the language of
the last message, at most one question per turn and only for a real
decision, one short sentence before a slow step and a progress line only at
a real milestone, a failure said in one sentence with what to do next, then
silence), and at the end of the call an optional written follow-up below a
line of `---` that is never spoken.
Under that contract, every speech path removes identifiers on its own
(`shared/spoken-identifiers.ts`: UUIDs, hashes, tokens, JWTs, `#1234`
numbers, `id: 42` labels; absolute and home paths keep their last name):
the page's sentence cleaner (`src/lib/voice-mode/spoken.ts`), the server's
speakable text (`server/tts/speech-text.ts`) and the iPhone's
(`SpokenText.speakableSentence`, same rules in Swift). The streaming
voice's appended words (`speakableDelta`) arrive in pieces that may cut a
word in two, so the server holds the last unfinished word of an open
utterance, and an `id:` label before it, until a space or a sentence end
follows or the utterance finishes (`splitHeldDelta`, at most 400
characters), then cleans it whole. The opening `say` of an answer is not
held: its first words are the call's first audio.
The contract is also held on the call's side, whatever the model wrote
(`src/lib/voice-mode/answer-budget.ts`, the iPhone's `AnswerBudget.swift`):
a call says at most four sentences of one answer (a line break after words
ends one too; a list number, an abbreviation or a decimal does not), and a
question ends what is said, so the person answers it. The cut keeps a
prefix of the text so far that only grows, so the answer still being
written is cut at the same place. The words after the cut stay in the
chat; after the sentence cap the call says once "The rest is written in
the chat." (`voiceMode.restInChat`, in the call's language), never after a
question or a barge-in. The live call, the older macOS call, a room call
and the iPhone apply it.
Numbers, times and dates are read the way a person says them, in the
language of the text (`server/tts/voice-reading.ts`, on every streaming
speech path): French text (`french-reading.ts`) reads "15:30" and "15 h 30"
as "15 heures 30", "09:00" as "9 heures", an ISO date "2026-10-18" as "18

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: The call button on an organization server
sections.text:
The client never decides alone: it asks `GET /api/bots/ /voice/status`
(again at each click while voice mode is unavailable, so a key just added
works at once). With a key the button opens the bar. Without one it shows
the speaker's access card in its popover ("You don't have xAI access for
voice mode: add your xAI key in Perspicax."; an admin also reads the
organization's key hint and gets "Open Settings > Connections"). If the
server cannot answer, the popover says so with the error and a retry. The
legacy call gate (macOS dictation, "Choose This computer") never shows on an
organization server.

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: Timings in the Events lens (2026-10-29)
sections.text:
Where the seconds of a spoken turn went shows in the thread's Events lens
as `runtime.notice` rows (`server/voice-timing.ts`), numbers only, never
the words: each call turn ("Voice turn: end of speech, speech to text,
send" from the page's `voiceCall.timing`, then "turn setup, engine (warm
or cold start), first words" from `server/voice-latency.ts`), each
streamed transcript (the final words after the page's finalize) and each
whole-recording upload (how long xAI took for how many seconds of audio).
A call turn sent early on its partial and sent again with its final words
(`reissue`, `call.ts`) interrupts the first one and sends the second:
the two requests race, and the final words can reach the running turn
just before the interrupt stops it. The interrupt names the utterance it
cancels (`expectedUtteranceId`); the call watchdog answers words of a
newer utterance stopped that way (`unansweredCallMessage`
`stoppedUtteranceId`), where they used to wait for the person's next
message (2026-10-29: 44 s, until they typed the question).

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: When xAI fails a request
sections.text:
xAI's refusal is never hidden behind "didn't come through" (2026-10-28):
- `server/tts/grok.ts` reads the status of a refused socket handshake (`ws`
 says "Unexpected server response: 429") and words it like an HTTP refusal:
 key or permissions (401, 403), credits (402), rate limit (429), xAI failing
 (5xx); a real network error stays "Could not reach Grok voice". xAI answers
 an invalid key with 400 "Incorrect API key provided" (checked
 2026-10-28), so the refusal's body is read too (REST, and the socket's
 `unexpected-response`), up to 2 KB, only to sort it: key, credits, rate
 limit. Another 400 keeps xAI's category ("Client specified an invalid
 argument"), never its message.
- Every 502 of a voice route answers `{ error, code: "voice_provider",
 failure, key, tried? }`, `failure` being `key`, `quota`, `busy`, `down`,
 `voice` or `other` (`grokVoiceFailure`), `key` the key it is about (its
 source and last four characters, `{ source: "voice-key" | "perspicax-key"
 | "org-key" | "server", last4 }`, never more) and `tried` every key refused
 on the way when more than one was. The server log says which request
 failed and on which key (`[voice-mode] xAI stream failed (speaker-key,
 person's voice key ···Wez8): ...`), never the key.
- The page tries a sentence once more after a busy or failing xAI or a
 stall (`streamVoiceModeSpeech`, 400 ms), then says the reason in the bar,
 naming the key and what to do about it when the server named one
 ("xAI has no credits left for your voice key ···Wez8. Add credits to that
 xAI account, or change the key in Settings > Models and voice > My voice
 keys.", `voiceMode.provider. .named`, `voiceMode.key.*`,
 `voiceMode.keyAction.*`), else the plain line
 (`voiceMode.provider. `). That line goes away as soon as the voice
 is heard again; "Try again" is offered only for the microphone, the one
 thing it reopens (`voiceErrorNote` in `src/lib/voice-mode/failure.ts`).
 A 403 mid-call (no key serves the person any more) shows the access card
 in the bar, as before the call. The call's settings show which key the
 voice runs on ("Voice: xAI with your voice key ···Wez8",
 `voiceMode.keyLine`, from `status.key`).
- The bar's transcript shows the bot's words as they are said: the spoken
 part, without markdown (`transcriptText` in `src/lib/voice-mode/spoken.ts`,
 `SpokenText.transcriptText` on iOS).
- iOS (`CallProvider.choose`): with voice mode available, the call hears
 through xAI on the server (POST /voice/transcribe) and speaks with xAI, the
 desktop's provider for that person; Apple's recognizer and voice are only
 the fallback when no voice provider is set up (a group call, the demo, a
 server without voice mode). The call's transcript header says which one
 and on which key ("Voice: xAI with your voice key ···Wez8",
 `VoiceWords.providerLine`). Since 2026-10-28 the status is asked twice
 and a server that cannot answer, or a refusal on a personal server, is
 said at the start of the call ("...

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: Who pays, and the key
sections.text:
The key never reaches the client. Order for the person who speaks
(`server/voice-mode.ts` `resolveVoiceKeys`, `server/voice-keys.ts`):
- Organization server: the xAI key they saved in Sagax for their own voice
 (Settings > Models and voice > My voice keys, `server/person-voice-keys.ts`,
 2026-10-28; it needs no grant of the organization's voice), else their own
 xAI key in Perspicax (provider `xai`), else the organization's xAI key (Settings > Models and voice, `config.xai.key`
 or `XAI_API_KEY`), else refused with an access card shown in their bar only,
 under the audience rule of every access card (`accessCardAudience`: the
 person it is about; the organization's key hint only for an admin).
 A disabled person is refused and never falls back on the organization.
- Solo server: the server's xAI key.
The key that has funds (2026-10-28). Every request starts with the
first key of that order. When xAI refuses it for credits (`quota`) or for
the key itself (`key`: invalid, revoked, no voice permission), the next key
is tried at once (`withVoiceKeys`), on REST and on the sockets alike; a
rate limit, xAI down or an unknown voice stays with the key that got it,
another key would not help. The refusal is remembered per person for
`VOICE_KEY_REFUSAL_TTL_MS` (5 minutes), so the following sentences skip
straight to the key that works instead of paying a 402 round trip each,
and a refilled key is tried first again after that. The answer names the
key that served (`x-voice-key: perspicax-key:c0Je` on HTTP, `key` on the
sockets' `ready` frame) and the ones skipped (`x-voice-key-skipped:
voice-key:Wez8:quota`, `skipped`); the page says it once in the bar ("your
voice key ···Wez8 was refused (no credits). The voice now runs on your xAI
key in Perspicax ···c0Je.", `voiceMode.keyFallback`), never a silent
switch. `GET /voice/status` lists every key in its order with the refusals
remembered (`keys[].refused`) and the one the next request starts with
(`key`). If Perspicax cannot be reached, the person's own voice key still
serves; `perspicax_unreachable` is refused only when no other key exists.
Since 2026-10-14 Grok voice has no key of its own: it uses the xAI key, the
one bots on Grok use. A Grok voice key saved by an older build
(`config.tts.xaiKey`, `SAGAX_XAI_VOICE_KEY`, the desktop's `xaiVoiceKey`)
becomes the xAI key when none is saved; otherwise the xAI key stays and the
duplicate is dropped. Both cases are logged without the value
(`server/config.ts` `migrateGrokVoiceKey`, `electron/workspace-credentials.mjs`
`foldGrokVoiceCredential`).
Each speak and transcribe is booked in the usage ledger (`driverKind`
`xai-voice`, model `grok-tts` or `grok-stt`, `access` = the via,
`payerPrincipalId` when the speaker's own key paid; no price: unpriced).
Perspicax lists `xai` keys since its migration 0043 (its provider keys are
`anthropic`, `openai`, `xai`, `google` and `moonshot`, on the console page

sections.title: Voice mode with xAI: xAI endpoints and key
sections.text:
An xAI API key from console.x.ai with access to the voice endpoints:
- Streaming speech to text, `wss://api.x.ai/v1/stt` (query `model`,
 `encoding=pcm`, `sample_rate=16000`, `interim_results`, `endpointing`,
 `language`, `format` (only with a language), `filler_words=true`,
 `keyterm`, `smart_turn=0.9`, `smart_turn_timeout=5000`; events
 `transcript.created`, `transcript.partial` with `is_final`,
 `speech_final` and `end_of_turn_confidence`, `transcript.done`;
 `{"type":"finalize"}` ends an utterance and the session goes on), and
 `POST https://api.x.ai/v1/stt` (multipart `language`, `format`,
 `filler_words`, `keyterm`, then `file` last) for a whole turn; the
 route hands back its words without fillers:
- `POST https://api.x.ai/v1/tts` (`text`, `voice_id`, `language`, `speed`
 0.7 to 1.5, `output_format` `{codec: "pcm", sample_rate: 24000}` for a live
 call; the response body streams the audio as it is made), and
 `GET https://api.x.ai/v1/tts/voices`:
 .
- Streaming text to speech, `wss://api.x.ai/v1/tts` (query `language`,
 `voice`, `codec=pcm`, `sample_rate=24000`, `speed`,
 `optimize_streaming_latency=2`; client `text.delta`, `text.done`,
 `text.clear`; server `audio.delta` base64, `audio.done`, `audio.clear`,
 `error`; the socket stays open between utterances):
 .
 The live call's "Streaming voice" uses it; POST `/v1/tts` is its fallback.
xAI's ephemeral client secrets (`POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets`,
 )
open only the realtime speech-to-speech agent
( ), where
Grok answers by itself instead of the bot, its tools, approvals and memory;
voice mode never uses it. The key stays on the server: the page talks only to
the server's own voice routes.

sections.title: Voice in Sagax: Call mode
sections.text:
Half-duplex, on purpose. The dictation helper is `SFSpeechRecognizer` on raw
`AVAudioEngine` input with no acoustic echo cancellation. A microphone left open
through playback transcribes the bot's own voice back into the conversation and
the two of them talk forever. So the mic is live only when the bot is not
speaking, and interrupting is a tap, the Space bar, or Escape. Full-duplex
barge-in needs AEC on the capture path — a real follow-up, not a footnote.
Turn detection stays native and local. A buffer-backed
`SFSpeechRecognizer` does not emit `isFinal` just because the speaker becomes
quiet; it finalizes only after its audio stream ends. Call mode therefore starts
the native helper with a silence timeout. Once a non-empty transcript stops
changing for 850ms, the helper stops capture and calls `endAudio()`, which
produces the final transcript sent to the renderer. Composer dictation omits the
timeout and keeps its press-to-stop behavior. No cloud STT or bundled VAD model
is involved.
Narration is what makes it bearable. An agent turn is 5–60 seconds of tool
calls, and silence that long reads as a dropped call. Every activity chip the
harness narrates is read aloud as it happens. The phrase is computed once,
server-side, into `tool.spoken` at fold time — so the chip you see and the phrase
you hear cannot drift apart.
Approvals are spoken. A `request.opened` card is read out and answered with
"yes"/"no". Anything that is not clearly a decision is refused and re-asked:
consent must never be inferred from a sentence that merely contained the word
"sure". Non-permission questions are read too, and the next complete spoken
turn is returned as the answer, so an agent asking for input does not strand the
call behind an invisible card.
Latency, honestly. Endpointing is 300–700ms and time-to-first-byte is
~100–250ms, against an agent turn of 5–60s. The agent dominates by 50–100x, so
voice choice is a quality decision, not a latency one. The way to make a call
feel conversational is to put the bot you call on a fast model and let it
delegate real work to specialists over `ask_bot` — no new machinery required.

sections.title: Voice in Sagax: Failure boundaries
sections.text:
- Intentional microphone stops (playback, hang-up, or replacement) do not emit
 a natural `speech:end`; otherwise the renderer could reopen capture during
 the bot's audio.
- Call phases are updated synchronously alongside React state, so a helper exit
 in the same event-loop turn as a final transcript cannot observe a stale
 `listening` phase.
- Leaving the bot view owns and ends its call. A hidden overlay cannot leave a
 microphone session or a stale `currentCall` behind.
- Synthesis requests are abortable from the renderer and individual utterances
 are capped server-side to bound accidental hosted-voice spend.

sections.title: Voice in Sagax: Known gaps
sections.text:
- Take-turns calls are macOS-only, because dictation is. The voice half
 works everywhere. Live calls (GPT-Live, `server/live-call.ts`) need no
 dictation, so they work in the desktop app on any computer and on the
 phones, with the person's own OpenAI key. A Cloud's page, in a web browser
 or the desktop app, runs the same code, but no Live call has been made end
 to end on a real Cloud yet.
- Rooms don't speak yet, though per-bot voices already exist (`bot.voice`).
- No spend meter. ElevenLabs bills per character. Auto-speak is off by
 default partly for that reason, but the app should eventually show usage.
- No voice barge-in — see half-duplex above.

sections.title: Voice in Sagax: Rejected
sections.text:
| Option | Why not |
 
| OS voices (macOS/Windows) | Audibly synthetic; would cheapen the feature |
| Piper | Same complaint, one tier up |
| Kokoro-82M in the renderer | Genuinely good and free, but it is a second provider, a 2.2MB chunk, an ONNX runtime and a first-run model download. Simplicity won. |
| Cartesia | Cheaper and faster to first byte, but a second provider earns its keep only once one is not enough |
| ElevenLabs Agents | Its custom-LLM `cascade_timeout_seconds` maxes at 15s and agent turns exceed that; it also wants to own turn-taking and tool calls, which is what the harness owns |
| OpenAI Realtime / Gemini Live (speech-to-speech) | They replace the brain, and the brain being Claude Code on your own machine *is* the product. (Later: GPT-Live's *client delegation* keeps the bot as the brain, so it became the optional Live call mode — see `server/live-call.ts`.) |

sections.title: Voice in Sagax: Shape
sections.text:
One voice provider: ElevenLabs, bring your own key. No local model, no
second provider, no fallback ladder — if there is no key, voice is off and the
buttons say so.

sections.title: Voice in Sagax: The spoken register
sections.text:
The half that decides whether this is pleasant. Agents write for a screen:
fenced code, file paths, tables, link soup. Read aloud verbatim, a diff is four
minutes of punctuation and `server/drivers/acp/core.ts` is "server slash drivers
slash a c p slash core dot t s".
`speech-text.ts` says the prose, names the artifacts, drops the syntax. It also
splits into utterances, because that is the unit of work — one request, one clip,
and the client fetches the next while the current one plays. One request per
utterance rather than the streaming-input WebSocket: same perceived latency, far
fewer moving parts, and no socket to leak when a turn is interrupted.

sections.title: Voice in Sagax
sections.text:
Historical decision doc, 2026-08-14. It records the original ElevenLabs-only
shape; the current product also supports Fish Audio, built-in Mac voices, and
local Chatterbox. See the current voice guide,
and voice mode with xAI for the floating voice bar.

sections.title: Voice in Sagax: Why the key stays on the harness
sections.text:
The renderer never talks to ElevenLabs. `GET /api/config` reports
configured-or-not booleans and nothing else, which is the same rule every other
credential follows, and it is worth more than a saved round trip. So the app
asks the harness for audio and the harness holds the key.
Two states worth distinguishing, because they need different instructions:
`configured` (a key is saved) and `ready` (a key *and* a chosen voice). Speaking
without either throws `NoVoiceConfigured`, which the route turns into a 409 —
"you haven't set this up" is not a provider failure and should not look like one.

sections.title: Signed bot visits
sections.text:
The bot's own browser attaches a signature to the pages it opens, so a site
that wants to can check the visit came from that bot. This is not a login
and not a way around one. Sagax never reads the signature as a session, and
the headers are never `Authorization` or `Cookie`. A saved login still uses
the existing login card. The person's own browser (attached from outside)
is not signed.
The signature is on unless that person turns it off.
 
A missing choice means on. On an organization server each person has their
own key and their own switch. Another member cannot turn it off or read the
private key. The answer is the public key id and a one-key directory. The
private key stays sealed with the vault key in `web-bot-auth-key.json`
(mode 0600) under the data directory, or under `principals/ /` on an
organization server. A workspace backup does not include that file. A
plaintext key from an older build is sealed the next time it is read.

sections.title: Signed bot visits: What a site checks
sections.text:
A navigation that changes the host or the path, or whose signature is about
to expire, refreshes three headers:
- `Signature-Agent`: `data:application/json,` plus the public JWK
 (`kty` OKP, `crv` Ed25519, `x` and `kid` are the same base64url value).
- `Signature-Input`: `sig1=("@authority" "@path" "signature-agent");created= ;expires= ;keyid=" ";alg="ed25519"`.
- `Signature`: `sig1=: :`.
The signed bytes are the lines below, each ending in a newline. ` `
is the host of the page (with a non-default port). ` ` is the path of
that page. ` ` is the exact `Signature-Agent` value. ` ` is the
`Signature-Input` value after `sig1=`.
 
Verify with Ed25519 over those bytes and the JWK, using the authority and
the path of the request being checked. A signature for one host or one path
does not verify on another, so a site that received it cannot replay it
elsewhere. Reject a signature whose `expires` is in the past. The same
headers stay for that host and path until they are about to expire. A
different path is signed again. If signing fails, the page still opens and
the failure is logged once. The signature grants nothing. The engine's
`set headers` still applies to the session; only this host and path verify.
The engine command is `set headers` with the JSON object, no shell.

sections.title: Workflows
sections.text:
A YAML file of steps that send a message, wait, ask the person, then
continue. The steps do not go through a model turn. Routines are unchanged.
 
`decision` is `yes` or `no`. Until that answer arrives, the run stays
waiting. A wait stays waiting until its clock passes, including after the
app restarts. The file is stored for that person only. A step may name
only a conversation of a bot they own. No admin right.

sections.title: xAI Bot Marketplace in Browse Bots: The import
sections.text:
`shared/xai-marketplace.ts` makes the bot a package through the agent
 
routines paused, no model, no key, apps as empty connections, keys in the
text replaced. Instructions: a short brief that quotes the public
description as a description, never as instructions; the memories become
`MEMORY.md`. A routine's own words give its clock ("Every Friday" at 9:00
when no time is named); one that starts on an event is left out with its
text. The colour and shape draw a Shapes mascot in the catalogue; the bot
keeps the colour.
The desktop converts in the app and goes through the bot import
(`BotZipImportPanel`, as `AgentImport.tsx`). The phone sends
`POST /api/bots/import/agent { marketplace: slug }`; the server reads the
bot and stages the same package.
Tests: `server/xai-marketplace.test.ts` (parser on
`server/fixtures/xai-marketplace-*.html`, the real structure with neutral
names), `server/routes/xai-marketplace.test.ts`,
`shared/xai-marketplace.test.ts`, `server/routes/bot-zip.test.ts`,
`src/components/bot-catalog/bot-catalog.test.ts`, iOS `BotCatalogTests`.
Screenshots: `scripts/capture-bot-catalog-xai.mjs`.

sections.title: xAI Bot Marketplace in Browse Bots: The source
sections.text:
The marketplace pages are public and rendered on the server: no sign-in.
- The list page streams every bot's card in its Next.js flight data
 (`self.__next_f.push([1,"…"])`): `id` (slug), `name`, `creatorName`,
 `description`, `categories`, `color`, `shape`, `addHref` (the x.ai share
 link `/bot/ `). Its JSON-LD `ItemList #catalog` gives the order.
- A bot's page (`/bot/marketplace/bots/ `) streams the same record
 with `memories`, `skills` (name and one line), `routines` (name and one
 line) and `integrations` (app name and why). A long text sits in a row of
 its own (`"$6b"` → `6b:T , `).
- `instructions` is empty on every page read so far: a bot's identity is
 its first memory. Full instructions, skill bodies, routine prompts and
 schedules stay inside the x.ai app.
`server/xai-marketplace.ts` reads both (x.ai only, redirects that stay on
x.ai, 20 s, 4 MB), keeps them six hours, and answers through
`GET /api/team-library/xai[?refresh=1]` and
`GET /api/team-library/xai/bots/:slug` (`server/routes/xai-marketplace.ts`).
A failure is a code, never x.ai's error: `xai_unreachable`, `xai_format`
(the page changed), `xai_blocked` (401, 403, 429 or a redirect off x.ai,
such as a sign-in), `xai_not_found`. A refresh that fails keeps the list
read earlier (`stale`).

sections.title: xAI Bot Marketplace in Browse Bots
sections.text:
Browse Bots lists the bots of the official xAI Bot Marketplace
(https://x.ai/bot/marketplace) in a section of its own, xAI Bot
Marketplace, beside Templates. A click opens the bot and its import
preview; Add makes it a new Sagax bot.

sections.title: Invisible deploys (zero downtime for people): 1. Server graceful shutdown
sections.text:
On `SIGTERM` / `SIGINT` (`server/graceful-shutdown.ts`, wired in
`server/index.ts`):
1. Mark probes unready (`markShuttingDown`): `/healthz` and `/api/health`
 answer 503 so the edge stops routing.
2. Close live SSE streams. Clients reconnect with their cursor
 (`?since=` / `Last-Event-ID`); the edge holds those reconnects.
3. Drain in-flight turns for a bounded time
 (`SAGAX_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS`, default 5 s on a server, 0 under the
 desktop app).
4. Stop accepting and finish in-flight HTTP
 (`server/http-shutdown.ts`), then flush durable state (bus, sessions,
 ledgers) and exit.
Runtime state is already durable on disk. Interrupted turns resume once
at the next start (`server/interrupted-turns.ts`).
Raise `SAGAX_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS` together with the container stop grace
period (Compose `stop_grace_period`, k8s `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`)
when turns need longer to land.

sections.title: Invisible deploys (zero downtime for people): 2. Caddy holds requests during the restart
sections.text:
Every Caddyfile we ship (`deploy/Caddyfile`, `install.sh`,
`server/caddy.ts`, `server/fleet.ts`, helm configmap, local/podman)
configures the reverse proxy to wait instead of 502 while the single
upstream is gone:
- `lb_try_duration 25s` / `lb_try_interval 250ms`
- passive: `fail_duration 10s`, `unhealthy_status 502 503`
- active: `health_uri /healthz`, `health_interval 2s`, `health_timeout 1s`
- app path keeps `flush_interval -1` for SSE
Caddy retries selecting a healthy upstream for that window. People see a
pause, not an error page.

sections.title: Invisible deploys (zero downtime for people): 3. Clients stay calm and resume the stream
sections.text:
Desktop / web (`src/`):
- Live events already reconnect with backoff and the cursor
 (`src/lib/live-events.ts`).
- While the stream is down for under 30 s after a live session, the UI
 shows Reconnecting… (`ChatReconnectBanner`) and suppresses error
 toasts for 502/503/connection refused (`src/lib/deploy-reconnect.ts`).
iOS (`ios/`):
- Stream resume from cursor is unchanged (`Client.events(since:)`,
 `Session`).
- Gateway 502/503/504 without another route show Reconnecting…
 (`ConnectionAdvice`); the status banner stays calm.
Companion sidecar:
- `ECONNREFUSED` / `ECONNRESET` to the harness answer 503 with a
 reconnecting message so the phone retries instead of toasting a hard
 failure.

sections.title: Invisible deploys (zero downtime for people): Deploy procedures
sections.text:
### Single VM (Docker / install.sh / `serve --domain`)
Caddy hold is the path. Typical update:
 
The old process gets `SIGTERM`, drains, exits. Caddy holds new requests
until `/healthz` is 200 again. Do not publish the app port without Caddy
in front.
### AKS / Kubernetes (helm chart under `deploy/k8s/helm/server`)
- Readiness probe: `GET /api/health` on the app port (already in the
 chart). During shutdown it returns 503 so the pod leaves the Service
 endpoints before exit.
- `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 40` covers drain + cleanup.
- Strategy:
- replicas > 1: `RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable: 0` (new pod
 ready before an old one is removed).
- replicas = 1 with a ReadWriteOnce PVC: `Recreate` (two pods cannot
 share that volume). Rely on Caddy's hold inside the pod (edge
 container) for the brief gap, same as a single VM.
Set `replicas` in values when the data volume and architecture allow more
than one server process. This chart never applies itself; operators apply
a rendered manifest.
### What not to do
- Do not run deploy scripts against live hosts from an agent session
 without an explicit operator GO.
- Do not skip Caddy (or an equivalent hold) in front of a public URL.
- Do not lower `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` below the drain + cleanup
 budget.

sections.title: Invisible deploys (zero downtime for people)
sections.text:
A Sagax restart used to show people errors: the process stopped accepting,
Caddy answered 502, and clients toasted a failure. Deploys should stay
invisible for a short restart (under about 30 seconds).
Three layers work together.

sections.title: What a member must ask an admin for
sections.keywords: admin administrateur demander ask permission droit right membre member refuse refused bloque blocked
sections.text: On an organization server a member asks an admin for: host-level bot tools (a write through act, including settings and plugins, or act on someone else's bot, add_mcp_server, attach_file, vm_exec, the cloud agent tools), a command on the organization's server itself (the engine's host shell), Full access, organization engines such as Voice mode (xAI), backups, Experimental features and Connected apps, and server settings. A member does NOT need an admin for a read-only act on their own bot, to run commands on the bot's own computer (its server environment, Local VM, This computer or cloud computer), or to create a webhook on the bot's own computer: those are the owner's own. The admin grants rights in the Perspicax console > Access > Bot rights, per person or team; a pending admin approval shows in Perspicax To do (À traiter).

sections.title: Stop asking approval for every command (approval mode, Full access)
sections.where: the icon left of the message field, or Edit bot > Security > Permissions
sections.access: the person, or their Primary Bot when they ask it (sagax_settings with quote); organization: Full access off until an admin allows it, and Ask/Auto choice needs bots.approvalLevel (off for members by default)
sections.keywords: approbation approval approuver approve demander ask auto full access acces complet permission commande command carte card mode
sections.text: The person chooses the bot's approval level: the icon left of the message field, or Edit bot > Security > Permissions. The level belongs to the bot: every conversation, routine and delegated run uses its current level, and a conversation keeps its own only when the person chose one in it. Approve for me (Approuver à ma place) uses the provider's automatic review (Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok) to approve routine actions and ask about others; Full access (Accès complet) runs commands and edits without cards, set from the packaged desktop app only; real questions and missing credentials still ask. Custom auto-review rules can allow specific commands. On an organization server Full access stays off until an admin turns on Allow full access (Settings > Organization, or Perspicax Settings > Bots > Policies), and a member needs bots.approvalLevel (Perspicax Access > Bot rights) to switch between Ask and Auto.

sections.title: Attach a large file or retry an interrupted upload
sections.keywords: attachment upload retry interrupted large file video fichier piece jointe televersement reprendre reessayer
sections.text: Attach or drop a file in the composer. Documents, audio and archives accept up to 250 MB each; videos accept up to 1 GB. Pictures keep 32 MB on a shared host and 90 MB on a solo host. Files larger than 4 MB upload in resumable chunks with progress. Removing the chip cancels the upload; Retry upload resumes the acknowledged bytes of that same file, including after the server restarts. The file is committed only after its content checks pass. Existing buffered previews have a separate 25 MB shared or 90 MB solo limit. Archives keep their unpacked-size and path rules. No extra administrator action is needed to attach your files.

One bot: its actions menu > Export the bot (.zip), optionally with its conversations. On an organization server the page needs the backup.workspace permission, and restoring stays with admins.

A confidential conversation is kept to its owner: other people, admins and bots outside it do not read it, and it is answered in the Sagax app only. On an organization server an admin may make new threads confidential by default (Settings > Organization). A thread working in a shared folder cannot be converted.

Only on the person's own request, at most 6 bots made by bots per person per hour. Below Full access the person approves a card; the new bot starts with connected apps and automatic approvals off. On an organization server a member creates bots for themselves only (permission bots.create, on by default). The person can always create one from the sidebar.

sections.title: Install a plugin for a bot
sections.where: sidebar Capabilities (Capacités), scope For <bot> (Pour <bot>)
sections.access: the bot's owner or someone who manages it; organization: a write waits for an admin, and an admin may limit marketplaces
sections.keywords: plugin plugins greffon installer install marketplace extension ajouter
sections.text: Yes, a bot can install a plugin itself with the act tool and its plugins parameter: list, addMarketplace, install (also updates), setEnabled, uninstall, removeMarketplace. Each write waits for the person's Allow on a card unless the bot's approval mode is auto or full. On an organization server a write (install, enable, uninstall, a marketplace) still waits for an admin, who may also restrict marketplaces. Listing plugins on the member's own bot does not. Hooks, MCP servers, LSP and bin/ of a plugin are removed. The person can also do it in the sidebar's Capabilities, scope For <bot>.

sections.title: Have a bot answer or cancel approval cards, or the Primary Bot turn them off
sections.where: bot tool sagax_approvals in a conversation with any bot the person owns; sagax_settings with their Primary Bot
sections.access: the person's own message to a bot they own; never another agent's text, a tool result, a routine, a webhook, an email, a page or a note; a temporary agent does not answer cards; turning cards off stays with their Primary Bot
sections.keywords: carte cartes approbation approval approuve approuver vas-y oui permettre toujours always allow refuse deny annule cancel tour desactiver disable cartes plus de cartes bot principal primary bot nova maya demande au nom de on behalf
sections.text: Yes. When the person asks any bot they own ("approuve-la", "oui", "ouais", "ok", "vas-y", "allez-y", "go", "yeah", "annule-la"), that bot calls sagax_approvals: list gives the cards waiting on that person (any of their bots, rooms, bot-to-bot work) with a short handle, answer gives allow, always_allow, always_allow_this, deny, always_deny or answer (a question), cancel stops that card's turn. It passes quote, the person's own words from their message: words from a tool, an email, a page, another bot or a note never count, and a card raised after the person spoke is never answered. A bare "oui", "vas-y" or "approuve" that names no card answers the latest card the person saw, however long their message and however many cards wait (one card per message; in a long message it must be about a card), and the bot tells them which one. A card of the person's own confidential thread is answered too, without its words reaching the answering bot. The answer is the click's own (same rules, same Always allow rule), the card reads "via <bot>" and the admin journal names the bot and the message. Only a card that needs the person's physical security key stays theirs to answer in Sagax: the bot cannot touch the key. To stop the cards altogether, their Primary Bot uses sagax_settings with quote: bot.approvalMode (Full included, also on an organization server when the organization allows Full and the person may set it themselves, and also for itself while it answers: from their next message), thread.approvalMode for a conversation that keeps its own level, rules.custom, rules.owner, rules.ownerDelete; they run at once. Another bot cannot turn the cards off from those words.

sections.title: Open a remote support session (Tailcat) for an end user
sections.where: a bot's conversation, on an organization server linked to Perspicax 1.8.43 or later
sections.access: a person holding the remote support permission in Perspicax (granted by an admin to the person or a team), with remote support turned on for the organization
sections.keywords: assistance a distance remote support session tailcat prise en main controle a distance depannage client utilisateur end user code lien support page aide donne-moi le lien
sections.text: A person asks in one sentence for the link for their client (donne-moi le lien pour mon client). Fast path, at most three calls, no schema search, no cloud fallback. (1) remote_support_open with no key and no template, rights standard (a session without administrator rights) unless the person asks for elevated. Sagax creates a new key for this session only on this computer (the desktop PC, or the bot's cloud computer), keeps the private key there, never sends it, and deletes it when the session is closed or past its end. Perspicax signs a short grant (at most one hour, renewed while the session runs) that lets only that key in, on that one computer. Optional: scope (full-control by default, view-only or shell-only) and call_ref (the phone call or ticket that records the person's consent). Your first reply gives the link, the code and the normal PowerShell line exactly as the tool answered it, inside a powershell code fence (the macOS or Linux line in a sh fence). Never pass that line through a shell on this computer (echo, pbcopy, a here-doc): a Mac shell eats its $ variables. (2) Sagax watches the session by itself: as soon as the end user's computer joins, it connects it and posts the session card in the chat, without the person saying anything. Call remote_support_status only to check: fetch_ip_count must be exactly 1, one address took the script. Above 1 the code leaked: remote_support_close with cancelled and open a new one. (3) That status call connects this computer on the technician side with the local key and marks the session connected. If it still says started, call it once more. The session then appears by itself in the bot panel (Remote sessions, Sessions à distance) and as a card in the chat: computer, user, rights, code, serial, model, processor, memory, disk, with Shell, Send a file and Download. Prendre le contrôle shows the screen in the Computer tab. Do not write a screenshot (jpg or png) to the Desktop or anywhere else, and do not open Preview: the screen is drawn in Sagax. Never expose the person's own computer: no tailcat serve, no exit node, no file sharing, no tunnel back to it. Do not ask anyone for a nodekey. Sagax ships tailcat 0.7.0 beside the app and in the server image. Do not download tailcat and do not copy it into a system directory. The address stays on this computer and is not repeated. Defaults: the technician shown is the person's name and the organization, the session ends in 2 hours (never past 24), the support page detects the OS. Always close at the end (ended, or cancelled if it never connected). The tools need a Perspicax profile mounted for the person speaking. remote_support_disabled means an admin has not turned remote support on.

sections.title: Create a routine (every morning, every weekday)
sections.where: bot tool propose_routine; also Automations in the account menu
sections.keywords: routine creer create planifier schedule chaque matin every morning 8h cron recurring recurrente tache task
sections.text: Yes: propose_routine with a cron schedule and an IANA time zone. A routine for the bot itself applies at once with an Undo, at any approval level (up to 20 enabled routines). A routine for another bot stays a card the person confirms, unless Full access is on. The person can also create and edit routines in Automations (account menu).

sections.title: Sort routines into folders
sections.where: bot panel > Details > Routines; bot tools propose_routine and propose_routine_action (folder)
sections.keywords: routine routines dossier dossiers folder folders ranger trier sort prefix prefixe groupe group organiser organize
sections.text: Yes: a bot's routines can sit in folders. In the bot's panel > Details > Routines, a row's menu (right click or its ...) has Move to folder, New folder... and Remove from folder; a folder's header folds, and its menu renames, reorders, pauses or resumes the whole folder, or deletes the folder (its routines stay, in no folder). When titles start with [Name], a line offers Sort by prefix once, with an Undo. A bot files its own routine with folder on propose_routine or propose_routine_action (null takes it out) and sees it in list_routines; never write the folder as a [Prefix] in the name. The person does it on their own bots, no admin.

sections.title: Where routines are
sections.where: account menu (avatar, bottom of the sidebar) > Automations (Automatisations); a bot's panel > Details > Routines
sections.keywords: routines routine ou sont where automations automatisations calendrier calendar planifiees scheduled
sections.text: In Sagax: the account menu (the person's avatar at the bottom of the sidebar) > Automations opens the routines calendar (upcoming runs, webhooks). One bot's routines are in its panel > Details > Routines, with an on/off switch per routine. A bot reads its own with list_routines and runs one with run_routine. On an organization server, the Perspicax console also lists them: Bots > Routines (/sagax/routines), for every person (their own).

sections.title: Change any setting through a bot
sections.where: bot tool sagax_settings; the same settings on screen (bot editor, Automations, Settings)
sections.access: the person speaking, with their own rights: a member cannot do through a bot what they cannot do by hand
sections.keywords: reglage reglages setting settings modifier changer change niveau approbation approval approuver pour moi auto modele model effort routine horaire schedule fil thread section geree managed built-in persona mascotte skin apparence notifications coffre vault organisation organization
sections.text: Yes: every setting is an action. A bot calls sagax_settings: action list (with a family: bot, thread, routine, group, section, rules, account, appearance, notifications, models, connections, credentials, server, organization, computer) gives the keys, get reads one, set changes it, through the same route the screen calls with the person's own session. The person's own bots and routines (model, effort, approval level up to the bot's own, managed teams such as Built-in, persona, look, routine schedule, conversation, on/off) change at once when the bot is at Approve for me or Full. A secret, a deletion, another person, several people or an organization setting waits for the person's Allow on a card, with their security key when they chose one for that kind; so does anything at Ask, and Full or Custom, unless the person's own Primary Bot makes the change because the person asked for it in their message (it passes quote, their own words): then approval levels (Full included, on an organization server too when the organization allows it and the person may set it themselves), Always allow rules and their removal run at once on any of the person's bots, the Primary Bot itself included (a key they chose, a secret, another person and the organization keep their card). Every change is written to the admin journal (setting.change). The full inventory is docs/settings-actions.md.

sections.title: Solo Sagax and organization (Perspicax) differences
sections.keywords: solo organisation organization perspicax admin membre member difference entreprise business
sections.text: Solo: a person's own Sagax; they hold every setting. Organization: a Sagax server linked to Perspicax (Sagax Business); people sign in with Perspicax, admins manage people, teams, bot rights, engines, routines and usage in the Perspicax console. A member's bot runs its commands, code and files on its OWN computer by default (its server environment (sagax-environment), its owner's own computer or Local VM (sagax-desktop), or its cloud computer), under the owner's own approval level, never assuming the shared organization server. The engine's host shell (a Bash or shell command on the shared server) is an admin's: only an admin targets the organization's server, so run commands on the bot's own computer instead. Host-level tools (add_mcp_server, attach_file, vm_exec, shared_computer, the cloud agent tools) also run only after an admin's approval. A read-only act on the member's own bot does not wait for an admin; a write through act, or act on someone else's bot, does. Perspicax also serves the organization's products (ConnectWise and others) to bots through api_list, api_search and the profile tools.

sections.title: Start work on an outside event (GitHub, webhook)
sections.where: account menu > Automations > Webhooks
sections.access: organization: server.settings (admin)
sections.keywords: webhook declencheur trigger github gitlab ticket issue evenement event slack sentry pagerduty linear demarrer start
sections.text: A webhook starts a task from outside: Automations (account menu) > Webhooks creates one with a bearer token shown once. Each webhook runs its task on the bot's own computer (This computer or its cloud computer), not on the organization's server. Typed triggers verified by the provider's own signature (GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Sentry, PagerDuty, Linear) exist on the server, but the app has no button to open their panel yet: say so rather than promising it. A bot cannot create either without the person's Allow (act on POST /api/webhooks). On an organization server a person creates and manages a webhook on the bot's own computer themselves, no admin and no server.settings needed; only a Microsoft trigger (it names a mailbox sign-in) or a webhook that would run on the organization's server is an admin's.

sections.keywords: note vocale voice note audio message vocal voix parler speak
sections.text: Yes with send_voice_note, but only when a voice is configured: a voice engine with its key and a voice for the bot or the app, and the bot's voice notes not turned off. Otherwise the tool is not offered. On an organization server using the organization's xAI key, only for people given Voice mode (xAI).

sections.title: Give voice mode (xAI) to a team or to people
sections.where: Perspicax console > Access > Bot rights (Accès > Droits sur les bots), tab Who has what (Qui a quoi), /sagax/permissions?tab=assign
sections.access: Perspicax admins only; a bot cannot do it
sections.keywords: voix vocal mode voix voice mode xai equipe team teams donner assigner moteur engine membres
sections.text: An admin does it in the Perspicax console: Access > Bot rights, tab Who has what; pick the teams or people, then give the engine Voice mode (xAI) (Mode voix (xAI)). A person's rights are the union of their own and their teams'. One person can also get it on their sheet. On the Sagax organization server the organization's xAI key then serves voice to admins and to the people given that engine. The personal xAI key is in Settings > Providers. In solo mode each person sets their own voice engine in Settings > Voice.

sections.title: Read a .zip or other archive
sections.keywords: zip archive archives tar gz 7z lire read fichier compresse decompresser unzip piece jointe attachment
sections.text: Yes, when the person attaches it in the chat: the bot gets the archive and a manifest of its files (zip, tar, tar.gz, 7z), then reads the files with its tools. Solo: unpacked next to the upload. Organization: listed on the host, then copied and unpacked where the bot's tools run (its server environment, or the person's computer through the desktop app) at its first tool call. Limits: 5,000 files, 512 MB unpacked, 200:1 ratio.

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.13 (2026-10-28): English
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.13 fixes blank pages, reorganizes Settings and adds previews to the Library.
### Pages
- No more blank page: the card and the page show again on the desktop connected to the organization server.
### Settings
- Separate pages: Account, Security, Vault, Models and Voice each have their own page.
### Library
- Mini previews: every row shows a preview, with a Today group and a Show more button (web and iOS).
### Interface
- Shapes: the full shape set, a pumpkin and eyes that always stay straight.
- Header: the "Teammates working" indicator is removed.

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.13 (2026-10-28)
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.13 corrige les pages blanches, réorganise les Réglages et ajoute des aperçus dans la bibliothèque.
### Pages
- Plus de page blanche : la carte et la page s'affichent de nouveau sur le desktop connecté au serveur de l'organisation.
### Réglages
- Pages distinctes : Compte, Sécurité, Coffre, Modèles et Voix ont chacun leur page.
### Bibliothèque
- Mini-aperçus : chaque ligne montre un aperçu, avec un groupe Aujourd'hui et un bouton Afficher plus (web et iOS).
### Interface
- Formes : le jeu de formes complet, une citrouille et des yeux toujours droits.
- En-tête : l'indicateur « Teammates working » est retiré.

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.14 (2026-10-28): English
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.14 makes voice mode more reliable, simplifies Connect Apps and refreshes the interface.
### Voice
- Your key first: voice mode uses your personal voice key first.
- Clear errors: the real reason for a refusal is shown, and resuming works without "Try again".
- iOS on xAI: iOS voice goes through xAI, and Markdown is no longer read aloud.
### Connect Apps
- Sources: reduced to marketplaces.
- GitHub: a single connection, and the GitHub MCP now receives the token.
- Pages tab: a new tab, and "My accounts" becomes "Providers".
### Interface
- Geist font: Geist for the interface, Geist Mono for code.
- Bubbles: accent color for your messages, gray for the bot.
- + menu: Loop and Goal are removed.
- Pages: Markdown tables render in pages.

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.14 (2026-10-28)
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.14 fiabilise le mode voix, simplifie Connect Apps et rafraîchit l'interface.
### Voix
- Votre clé d'abord : le mode voix utilise votre clé vocale personnelle en premier.
- Erreur claire : la vraie raison d'un refus est affichée, et la reprise se fait sans « Try again ».
- iOS sur xAI : la voix iOS passe par xAI, et le Markdown n'est plus lu à voix haute.
### Connect Apps
- Sources : réduit aux marketplaces.
- GitHub : une seule connexion, et le MCP GitHub reçoit enfin le jeton.
- Onglet Pages : nouvel onglet, et « My accounts » devient « Providers ».
### Interface
- Police Geist : Geist pour l'interface, Geist Mono pour le code.
- Bulles : couleur d'accent pour vos messages, gris pour le bot.
- Menu + : Loop et Goal sont retirés.
- Pages : les tableaux Markdown s'affichent dans les pages.

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.15 (2026-10-29): English
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.15 gives each bot a single conversation, lets the bot change any setting for you, and adds published pages, split view and the daily brief.
### Conversations
- One conversation per bot: a single thread per bot, with the same rule on the server, desktop and iOS.
- Split view: several conversations side by side in one window.
- Text your bot: a text message becomes a turn of your conversation, and the reply comes back by text.
- Groups: the team goal and its result stay in the group conversation, and you can leave a group someone added you to.
- Between bots: no more row for an empty thread, and the sheet shows an empty state.
### Voice
- xAI key: voice picks the key that has funds and names the key source in every refusal.
- Dictation and playback on xAI: on desktop and iOS. On iOS, Apple's voice is only an announced fallback.
### The bot can do everything
- Settings by bots: the bot reads and changes every setting for you (engines, Claude account, workspace, secrets and purchases by reference), with no "person only" barrier.
- Open app: settings kept on the device go through the open app, on desktop and iPhone.
- Invisible browsing: web browsing happens out of sight by default, and control of this computer is announced with a Stop button.
- Computer control: tied to the server started by the desktop app.
- Lent screen: the real reason shows when the screen is taken, and stale locks are released.
- Daily brief: it really runs in the background, on by default, and arrives through Reach me.
- On the person's behalf: phone calls, GitHub tools and images use the account of the person in the turn, including for members' bots on an organization server.
- Lighter tools: the tool list loads by family.
### Published pages
- Reading: reading bar, Share and Download PDF outside the frame, and a working full screen.
- Comments: comments anchored in the page, real time and presence, notifications, and the bot reads and answers comments.
- Suggestions: edit suggestions on Markdown pages.
- Sharing: public link without sign-in, back to the page after sign-in, shared state per page.
- Style: bot pages and widgets take the app's style by default.
### Appearance
- Appearance page: full-width preview and four tabs (Mascot, Shape, Color, Skin).
- Mascots fixed: a single geometry and motions that keep the whole body together.
- Bot color: your bubble and the toggles take the bot's color.
- Dark theme: readable lists and disabled buttons without a gradient.
- iOS notifications: the bot's mascot on the phone and the watch.
### Routines and calendar
- Folders: drag a routine from one folder to another.
- Reliability: a lost reply no longer looks like a failure or creates a duplicate.
- Calendar: every run of the day, the history of a deleted routine, and a member sees and schedules their bots' calls.
- Display: quiet Paused or Running state, action bar folds to icons in a narrow panel.
### Connections

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.15 (2026-10-29)
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.15 donne une seule conversation par bot, laisse le bot tout régler à votre place et ajoute les pages publiées, la vue partagée et le brief du jour.
### Conversations
- Une conversation par bot : un seul fil par bot, avec la même règle sur le serveur, le bureau et iOS.
- Vue partagée : plusieurs conversations côte à côte dans une fenêtre.
- Texter son bot : un texto devient un tour de votre conversation, et la réponse revient par texto.
- Groupes : l'objectif d'équipe et son résultat restent dans la conversation du groupe, et on peut quitter un groupe où on a été ajouté.
- Entre bots : plus de ligne pour un fil vide, et la feuille montre un état vide.
### Voix
- Clé xAI : la voix prend la clé qui a des fonds et nomme la source de la clé dans chaque refus.
- Dictée et lecture sur xAI : sur le bureau et sur iOS. Sur iOS, la voix d'Apple n'est plus qu'un repli annoncé.
### Le bot peut tout faire
- Réglages par les bots : le bot lit et change chaque réglage pour vous (moteurs, compte Claude, lieu de travail, secrets et achats par référence), sans barrière « réservé à la personne ».
- App ouverte : les réglages gardés sur l'appareil passent par l'app ouverte, sur le bureau et l'iPhone.
- Navigation invisible : la navigation web se fait hors de vue par défaut, et le contrôle de cet ordinateur est annoncé avec un bouton Arrêter.
- Pilotage de l'ordinateur : lié au serveur lancé par l'app de bureau.
- Écran prêté : la vraie raison s'affiche quand l'écran est pris, et les verrous périmés sont libérés.
- Brief du jour : il roule vraiment en arrière-plan, actif par défaut, et arrive par Me joindre.
- Au nom de la personne : appels téléphoniques, outils GitHub et images utilisent le compte de la personne du tour, aussi pour les bots des membres sur un serveur d'organisation.
- Outils plus légers : la liste d'outils se charge par famille.
### Pages publiées
- Lecture : barre de lecture, Share et Download PDF hors du cadre, plein écran qui fonctionne.
- Commentaires : commentaires ancrés dans la page, temps réel et présence, notifications, et le bot lit les commentaires et y répond.
- Suggestions : suggestions de modification sur les pages Markdown.
- Partage : lien public sans connexion, retour à la page après la connexion, état partagé par page.
- Style : les pages et widgets des bots prennent le style de l'app par défaut.
### Apparence
- Page Apparence : aperçu pleine largeur et quatre onglets (Mascot, Shape, Color, Skin).
- Mascottes réparées : une seule géométrie et des mouvements qui gardent le corps entier.
- Couleur du bot : votre bulle et les interrupteurs prennent la couleur du bot.
- Thème sombre : listes lisibles et boutons désactivés sans dégradé.
- Notifications iOS : la mascotte du bot sur le téléphone et la montre.
### Routines et calendrier
- Dossiers : glisser une routine d'un dossier à l'autre.
- Fiabilité : une réponse perdue ne fait plus croire à un échec ni créer de doublon.

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.16 (2026-10-29): English
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.16 connects Grok and Claude as connectors with two accounts, picks the right model for each turn, and adds shopping, the vault and recall by meaning.
### Engines and connectors
- Grok and Claude connectors: two Grok accounts per person, transparent routing between engines, and a Connect Claude card.
- Automatic model: your turn runs on the tier your words ask for (short question, image, long read).
- Work style: every turn reads a "Work style" section (plan, persistence, search before asking, recovery after an error, concision).
- Chat never blocked: you can always type, even while an approval is pending.
### The bot does more
- Shopping: products as cards, order tracking and subscription templates.
- Vault: a credential is lent for a single turn, with a real Shop Pay or Link card.
- Recall by meaning: on by default, a local semantic index merged with full-text search.
- Don't finish until…: active check, bounded follow-ups, setting on desktop and iOS.
- "Working" line: the bot names the current step, with the same text on every engine.
- Show a process in my Chrome: a recorder in the real Chrome, replay out of sight or announced.
### Display
- Bubbles: the bot's exact accent and the accent button's ink.
- Connect Apps: the GitHub connection moves to the GitHub plugin page, a Bots tab and a single search.
- Split view: the same centered badge in each section, and a single panel, always on the right.
- Conversation between bots: same layout as a 1:1 chat.
- External agent over MCP: an AI client that talks to your bot over MCP gets its own agent-to-agent conversation, under its name, without notifying you.
### Security and fixes
- Sandboxes: sandboxes stay out of the control plane (API and kubelet).
- Scheduled calls: a member can no longer touch another member's scheduled calls.
- Incidents: a report copied into the conversation rings once, never when it is quiet.
- Issues: #1327, #1329.
- Test suite back to green.

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.16 (2026-10-29)
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.16 branche Grok et Claude comme connecteurs avec deux comptes, choisit le bon modèle pour chaque tour et ajoute le magasinage, le coffre et le rappel par le sens.
### Moteurs et connecteurs
- Connecteurs Grok et Claude : deux comptes Grok par personne, routage transparent entre les moteurs, et une carte Connecter Claude.
- Modèle automatique : votre tour roule sur le palier que vos mots demandent (question courte, image, longue lecture).
- Façon de travailler : chaque tour lit une section « Work style » (plan, persévérance, chercher avant de demander, reprise après une erreur, concision).
- Chat jamais bloqué : vous pouvez toujours écrire, même pendant une approbation en attente.
### Le bot fait plus
- Magasinage : produits en cartes, suivi de commande et gabarits d'abonnements.
- Coffre : un identifiant est prêté pour un seul tour, avec une vraie carte Shop Pay ou Link.
- Rappel par le sens : actif par défaut, un index sémantique local fusionné avec la recherche plein texte.
- Ne pas terminer tant que… : contrôle actif, relances bornées, réglage sur le bureau et iOS.
- Ligne « au travail » : le bot nomme l'étape en cours, avec le même texte sur tous les moteurs.
- Montrer une démarche dans mon Chrome : un enregistreur dans le vrai Chrome, relecture hors de vue ou annoncée.
### Affichage
- Bulles : l'accent exact du bot et l'encre du bouton d'accent.
- Connect Apps : la connexion GitHub déménage dans la page du plugin GitHub, un onglet Bots et une seule recherche.
- Vue partagée : la même pastille centrée dans chaque section, et un seul panneau, toujours à droite.
- Conversation entre bots : même mise en page qu'un chat 1:1.
- Agent externe par MCP : un client IA qui parle à votre bot par le MCP a sa propre conversation entre agents, à son nom, sans vous notifier.
### Sécurité et corrections
- Sandboxes : les sandboxes restent hors du plan de contrôle (API et kubelet).
- Appels planifiés : un membre ne touche plus les appels planifiés d'un autre membre.
- Incidents : un rapport copié dans la conversation sonne une fois, jamais s'il est calme.
- Issues : #1327, #1329.
- Suite de tests remise au vert.

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.17 (2026-10-29): English
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.17 rebuilds routines, lets your bot manage its memory, skills and plugins, and makes the chat calmer.
### Routines
- Routines rebuilt: a clear list, one page per routine, the detail of each run and its logs. Same model on desktop and iOS.
- Review your routines: the bot can review all your routines at once. An option you click counts as if you had typed it.
- Routine webhook: the bot can create a routine's webhook for you.
### Your bot does more
- Memory: the bot tidies its own topic files.
- Skills: the bot imports a skill from GitHub.
- Plugins and MCP: the bot adds and sets them up for you.
- Full context: when a conversation gets too long, the bot picks up in a fresh session on its own, without losing the thread.
### Display
- Chat: the thread stays at the bottom, even when a panel changes size.
- Task sheet: a clear header, what is waiting for you first, steps grouped.
- Sidebar: a simple dot marks what is unread, instead of a number.
- Published pages: the banner follows your theme, and a page's shared state is written according to the page and its sharing.
- iOS Connect apps: a Bots tab and a single search.
- Replies in red: a normal bot reply never shows as a red error card again, on desktop and iOS.
### Security and fixes
- Usage limit: when Claude says your usage limits are reached, Sagax recognizes it. It switches to another engine or simply tells you when the limit comes back, instead of an HTTP 400 error.
- Sandboxes: the node guard now tolerates the sandbox pool.
- README rewritten, with new screenshots.

sections.title: Sagax 0.8.17 (2026-10-29)
sections.text:
Sagax 0.8.17 refait les routines, laisse votre bot gérer sa mémoire, ses skills et ses plugins, et rend le chat plus calme.
### Routines
- Routines refaites : une liste claire, une page par routine, le détail de chaque exécution et ses journaux. Même modèle sur le bureau et sur iOS.
- Relire vos routines : le bot peut relire toutes vos routines d'un coup. Une option que vous cliquez compte comme si vous l'aviez écrite.
- Webhook de routine : le bot peut créer le webhook d'une routine pour vous.
### Votre bot fait plus
- Mémoire : le bot range lui-même ses fichiers de sujets.
- Skills : le bot importe un skill depuis GitHub.
- Plugins et MCP : le bot les ajoute et les règle pour vous.
- Contexte plein : quand une conversation devient trop longue, le bot reprend tout seul dans une session neuve, sans perdre le fil.
### Affichage
- Chat : le fil reste collé en bas, même quand un panneau change de taille.
- Feuille de tâche : un en-tête clair, ce qui vous attend en premier, les étapes regroupées.
- Barre latérale : un simple point signale ce qui n'est pas lu, au lieu d'un chiffre.
- Pages publiées : le bandeau suit votre thème, et l'état partagé d'une page s'écrit selon la page et son partage.
- iOS Connect apps : un onglet Bots et une seule recherche.
- Réponses en rouge : une réponse normale du bot ne s'affiche plus jamais comme une carte d'erreur rouge, sur le bureau et sur iOS.
### Sécurité et corrections
- Limite d'usage : quand Claude dit que vos limites d'usage sont atteintes, Sagax le reconnaît. Il passe à un autre moteur ou vous dit simplement quand la limite revient, au lieu d'une erreur HTTP 400.
- Sandboxes : la garde des noeuds tolère maintenant le pool des sandboxes.
- README refait, avec de nouvelles captures.
